title: Barkman Avenue local improvement: one written objection sent the borrowing to the Municipal Board
summary: Public hearing on Local Improvement Plan 2016-01 (By-law 2016) to rebuild three blocks of Barkman Avenue, with $1M of the $2.14M cost borrowed. Notices went out under the Municipal Act and one written objection was on file; nobody spoke at the hearing. Council gave first and second reading; because of the objection the borrowing went to the Manitoba Municipal Board, which approved it, and council gave third reading on Feb 16, 2016.
status_detail: Approved as proposed. One objector triggered a Municipal Board review (30-45 days per the city manager); the Board approved and third reading followed Feb 16, 2016.
figures: Project $2.14M; $1M borrowed over 5 years; $840,000 Canada-Manitoba Infrastructure Program; $300,000 Municipal Road Improvement Fund (transcript 2015-12-15 0:06:22).
reasons: notice-meets-act: Notices issued as required under the Municipal Act; recommended proceeding subject to the hearing and Municipal Board approval. (Troy Warkentin)
public: One registered written objection (author not named in the meeting); no one spoke at the hearing.
notes: Local-improvement (borrowing) hearing rather than a land-use hearing; included because it shows the objection threshold. The objector's identity and grounds are not stated in the transcript.

title: 2016: about 21 land-use hearings with no objectors, all approved where checked
themes: variance; conditional-use; rezoning; subdivision; notice; process
summary: Besides the contested files, council held about 21 land-use hearings in 2016 at which nobody objected (variances, conditional uses such as tattoo parlours, a hotel on PTH 52 and Menno Mart, the Park Hill school-site plan and rezoning, a sign amendment, a subdivision). At each, the city manager reported that notices had been issued under the Planning Act and whether any correspondence was received, and the chair asked three times for objectors. A few neighbours came only with questions or support (e.g. 490 Ash Avenue, whose applicant had visited six neighbours).
status_detail: All approved where the transcript shows the vote.
figures: Count from transcripts: Jan 19 (1), Feb 2 (2), May 17 (1), Jun 7 (1), Jul 19 (4), Aug 2 (1), Sep 6 (3), Sep 20 (3), Oct 18 (1), Nov 15 (2), Dec 6 (1), Dec 20 (1, three Park Hill files heard together) = 21.
reasons: staff-recommends: Approval recommended subject to any new information at the hearing. (Troy Warkentin)
public: None objected; neighbours at V-2016-05 (180 Main) and CU-2016-05 (hotel) asked questions only; the 490 Ash neighbour supported.
notes: Counts are from transcripts (no minutes for 2016) and may miss a file heard concurrently; not every vote was read in full.

title: 242-250 Hanover Street: 24-32 unit apartments approved over neighbours' objections (split vote)
summary: CASL Developments applied (CU-2016-02 and V-2016-01) to build two 3-storey apartment buildings in the C-1 transition zone on Hanover Street without the required ground-floor commercial. No written objections had been filed, but at least three neighbours across the street spoke: they objected to three storeys, the front parking lot and driveway, traffic and speed, old sewer capacity, park access and property values/taxes. The applicant said he had door-knocked neighbours and asked council to allow up to 32 units. Council approved both files as recommended.
status_detail: Conditional use and variance both approved as applied, subject to a development agreement. No conditions were added in response to the objectors; the applicant offered a park gate and screened garbage area verbally.
figures: 2 x 3-storey buildings, 24 units proposed, applicant asked for up to 32 (transcript 0:39:52); city manager estimated existing 3 houses at $600-700K assessment vs ~$3M for 30 units (0:56:33).
reasons: meets-the-plan: Multifamily is allowed as a conditional use in the transition zone; a commercial building could already go there and be taller. (Michael Zwaagstra); precedent: Council approved similar files (CU-2013-07, V2013-28). (Troy Warkentin); traffic-manageable: Downtown residents would walk more; speeding is a police matter. (John Fehr); staff-recommends: Recommended approval subject to a development agreement; sewer capacity is checked by engineering. (Troy Warkentin)
public: Three residents across the street (M.W., J.R., C.W.) raised height, parking lot in front, driveway safety, speeding, 60-year-old sewer, property values and taxes, and park access for a disabled neighbour. No written objections were registered before the meeting.
vote: CU carried with at least one Councillor Penner opposed (count not stated); variance carried
notes: Speaker labels in this file mix residents and the applicant; resident counts are approximate. Which Councillor Penner voted no is not determinable.

title: Lund Road rezoning (By-law 2015) finished after a Municipal Board hearing on objections
summary: A 2013 rezoning of land on Lund Road from M-1 industrial to RMD residential had drawn objections and gone to the Manitoba Municipal Board. With the Board's approval in hand, council gave third reading on Feb 2, 2016 and approved the 56-lot bare-land condominium subdivision on Apr 5, 2016.
status_detail: Approved as originally proposed after a roughly three-year Municipal Board process.
reasons: need-housing: Condominium units would be reasonably priced starter homes and a buffer to the industrial park. (Chris Goertzen)
public: Original objectors (2013) are not identified in the transcripts.
mover: not clear in transcript (third reading); Jac Siemens (subdivision)
notes: The 2013 hearing itself is outside this period and not transcribed.

title: Annual financial plan public hearings drew no public questions
summary: The 2016 (Feb 16) and 2017 (Feb 21) financial plans were presented at public hearings before adoption. In 2017 the mayor noted the largest turnout in some time, but no one from the gallery asked a question either year.
status_detail: Both plans adopted the same evening.
public: No public speakers recorded.

title: City objects to an RM of La Broquerie rezoning in the shared transition zone, citing no consultation
summary: The RM of La Broquerie received an application to rezone land just outside Steinbach to rural commercial/industrial. The city manager said it appeared contrary to the development plan and that the duty to consult in the transition zone was not met. Council authorized the city manager and planner to present the city's objection at the Municipal Board hearing on May 2, 2017. (Council had also received notice of an RM zoning by-law amendment on Feb 16, 2016 and discussed the transition zone again Oct 3, 2017.)
status_detail: Board hearing outcome not found in the transcripts.
notes: Inter-municipal notice, not residents; included as context on objection rights.

title: 26 Quail Ridge Place: oversized garage rebuild approved; neighbours' complaints about car repairs left to by-law enforcement
summary: Variance V-2016-02 to rebuild a 1,616 sq ft garage (900 allowed) destroyed by fire. Five letters arrived (one before the agenda, four after); three neighbours spoke. They did not object to the size but to commercial car repair, paint fumes, grinding noise and debris. Council approved the rebuild unchanged and told neighbours to use the home-based business and nuisance by-laws if commercial work continues.
status_detail: Approved as applied. No condition on use was attached; administration confirmed auto repair for others is prohibited as a home business and that no complaints were on file.
figures: 1,616 sq ft vs 900 sq ft maximum (transcript 0:04:41).
reasons: objections-not-planning-grounds: Size and activity are separate issues; activity is handled through complaints and by-laws. (Jac Siemens); property-rights: Building was legally built and lost to fire; same foundation and size. (Jac Siemens)
public: Neighbours L.K., M.D. and G.K. (plus letters) said they had no issue with the size but objected to commercial vehicle work, fumes and noise; the applicants' lawyer said existing by-laws give remedies.
notes: Mayor absent; deputy mayor chaired (not named in transcript).

title: Public engagement task force on the performing arts centre: phone, online and business surveys
summary: A council task force (Councillors Susan Penner, Cari Penner and Michael Zwaagstra) ran a scientific phone survey, an open online survey and a business survey on the proposed performing arts centre's scope, location and cost, and reported on Mar 15, 2016. Members said the consultant had never seen such a level of response.
status_detail: Report received; the project's cost later rose to $24.3M and was debated without further public consultation found in this period.
public: Survey respondents (results not read in detail on video).
notes: Topic overlaps with spending reports; listed here only as a consultation example.

title: Stonebridge Crossing (Bridge Park) rezoning approved with no site plan; lone objector did not attend Municipal Board
summary: Bridge Park Village Inc. asked to rezone 1.6 acres behind Albert Street homes from RLD to RMD for future seniors housing, with no concept plan. Two letters were on file and an Albert Street neighbour asked about height (up to 35 ft, 4 ft side yards), drainage and traffic, then registered as objecting. Councillors raised the missing plan and a possible 15-ft side yard condition but gave second reading without conditions, relying on the city's administrative infill policy. The objector did not appear at the Municipal Board hearing, which was cancelled, and council gave third reading on Feb 7, 2017.
status_detail: Rezoned as applied; no conditions. Future design left to administrative review under the infill policy, with no further council involvement (city manager, 2017-02-07).
figures: 1.6 acres; RMD max 3 storeys/about 35 ft, side yards 4 ft (transcript 0:46:19).
reasons: need-housing: Seniors housing is needed and belongs next to the existing campus; zoning ready for grant windows. (Michael Zwaagstra); meets-the-plan: Near a park, walkway and other multifamily; infill policy protects neighbours. (Chris Goertzen); already-consulted: Trusted Bridge Park and the infill policy's standards (third reading). (Susan Penner)
public: Two letters (contents not read out); Albert Street neighbour D.W. said the proposal was too vague and that 35 ft four feet off his yard was not compatible without a plan. He registered as objecting but did not attend the Municipal Board hearing.
mover: Michael Zwaagstra (2nd reading, Jul 19, 2016); Susan Penner (3rd reading, Feb 7, 2017)
notes: Mayor Goertzen absent Feb 7, 2017 (deputy mayor chaired).

title: Haven Group seniors high-rise at 90 Brant/Woodhaven: approved with a fence and access condition from objectors' letters
summary: By-law 2068 rezoned 159 and 163 Woodhaven Avenue and part of 90 Brant Street to RHD for a 5-storey seniors building (with variance V-2016-13). Two letters came in, one from the neighbouring condo corporation about access across its lot and one the day of the meeting about a fence and trees; a Woodhaven neighbour spoke about traffic, lost winter light and property values. Councillor Zwaagstra moved, as a friendly amendment, to make a 6-ft fence and Woodhaven access conditions of second reading. Second and third reading passed the same night.
status_detail: Approved with conditions answering the letter writers (6-ft fence; access via Woodhaven, not the condo lot). Light, traffic and value concerns were not addressed by conditions.
figures: 5 storeys; ground-level parkade, 1.5 stalls per unit (transcript 0:56:45).
reasons: need-housing: Additional seniors housing is needed. (Jac Siemens); traffic-manageable: Seniors drive less; quiet neighbours. (John Fehr); staff-recommends: No verified property-value impacts from multifamily in past rezonings. (Troy Warkentin)
public: Letters from the Charleswood condo corporation (access) and from W.F. and A.F. (fence, trees); Woodhaven neighbour M.H. raised traffic, light/shadow, foundations and property value, and said the applicant's answers eased some concerns.
mover: Jac Siemens (2nd reading); conditions by Michael Zwaagstra (friendly amendment)
vote: carried; third reading same night (seconded by a Councillor Penner); variance moved by John Fehr, seconded by Jac Siemens, carried
notes: First reading Sep 6, 2016 (moved by a Councillor Penner, seconded by Zwaagstra).

title: Mobile sign by-law changed after Chamber and sign businesses spoke at the hearing
summary: Zoning By-law amendment 2065 (mobile signs) had a public hearing Oct 18, 2016. The Steinbach Chamber of Commerce, Synex Manufacturing and Penner Signs raised setbacks, wording and illuminated signs; there were no formal objections. Council did not give second reading that night: it changed the front-yard setback to 1 ft, accepted the Chamber's wording fixes and sent illuminated signs back for review. The city manager warned that a material change needs a new or continued hearing. Second and third reading followed Nov 1, 2016, with illuminated mobile signs left for the next zoning review. (An earlier sign amendment, By-law 2066, drew no objectors on Jan 19, 2016.)
status_detail: Adopted with the setback change requested at the hearing; illuminated mobile signs deferred to the 18-24 month zoning review.
figures: Front yard setback changed from 10 ft to 1 ft, side yard 2 ft (transcript 2016-10-18 0:42:38).
reasons: precedent: Existing mobile signs already sit at those setbacks. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Business and Chamber representatives (organizations named: Steinbach Chamber of Commerce, Synex Manufacturing, Penner Signs). No residents spoke.
vote: carried (call for 'opposed' made; no dissent named)
notes: Business-to-council input, not neighbours; included as a hearing where input changed the outcome.

title: 295 Lowen Boulevard: parking variance denied, as staff and neighbours urged
summary: A developer asked to build 22 units with 26 parking stalls where 36 are required (V-2016-20), for rentals to Eden Health clients. Staff recommended denial; one email objection was on file and owners of the house next door objected in person (street parking, safety backing onto Lowen, a house they could not sell). Council denied the variance.
status_detail: Denied. The outcome matched the objectors, but administration had already recommended denial, so the objections were not the only factor.
figures: 22 units, 26 stalls vs 36 required; standard 1.5 stalls per unit plus 10% visitor (transcript 0:22:06). The site's original rezoning had gone to the Municipal Board on neighbours' objections (0:08:09).
reasons: staff-recommends: Parking standard exists for the long term; no guarantee future tenants need fewer stalls. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: One email objection; T.T., B.T. and C.N. (family owning the house next door) objected to reduced parking and described the project's effect on their property, asking for a buyout (not a planning matter, the chair said).

title: 24 Ellis Avenue six-plex: rezoning approved with a fence and 1.5-storey cap after a neighbour's privacy concern
summary: By-law 2075 rezoned 24 Ellis Avenue from RLD to RMD for a 6-unit building. One letter of objection was on file and the next-door owner asked for a full-length fence for privacy. Councillor Zwaagstra amended the motion to require a 6-ft wood fence and a 1.5-storey height limit. Because of the written objection, third reading waited; the objector did not take it to the Municipal Board and third reading passed Mar 21, 2017.
status_detail: Approved with conditions responding to the neighbour (fence, height cap).
figures: 6 units; 1.5 storeys; 6-ft wood fence (transcript 2017-02-21 0:20:27).
reasons: meets-the-plan: RMD already common on the street; trees saved, fence committed. (Earl Funk)
public: One written objection (author not named); neighbour M.R. said she did not necessarily object but wanted a fence along the whole property line. The applicant (D.S.-T.) had spoken to one neighbour only.
mover: Earl Funk (2nd reading); Michael Zwaagstra (3rd reading)
notes: First reading Jan 17, 2017.

title: 2017: about 21 land-use hearings with no objectors; two denied, one approved against staff advice
summary: About 21 hearings in 2017 had no objectors (mostly variances, signs, a daycare, Taves rezoning on By-law 2080). Most were approved. Council denied V-2017-27 (188-190 Chapel Drive parking) when no applicant appeared, and approved V-2017-26 (paving) against staff advice (see separate item). The Oct 17, 2017 hearing on 209 Stonebridge Crossing (By-law 2086) and the Apr 4, 2017 meeting are not transcribed.
status_detail: Approved in most cases; V-2017-27 denied.
figures: Count from transcripts: Jan 17 (3), Feb 21 (1), Apr 18 (1), May 2 (3), May 16 (2), Jun 20 (1), Jul 4 (1), Jul 18 (1), Aug 1 (2), Aug 15 (2), Nov 7 (1), Dec 5 (1), Dec 19 (2) = 21.
public: None objected.
resolution_no: R17-142 (V-2017-11, Jul 18; moved John Fehr, seconded Earl Funk, unanimous per minutes)
notes: Counts approximate.

title: 333 Lowen Boulevard: first residential mixed-use rezoning and 120-ft height approved over Albert Street objections
summary: By-law 2082 rezoned the former clinic site from C-4 to RMX and variance V-2017-13 sought a 120-ft building where 85 ft is allowed, for personal care beds, supportive living and apartments. One letter objected to the rezoning; at least five Albert Street residents spoke about parking, traffic, child safety, sidewalks, property values, privacy and especially height. Council gave second reading Jul 18 and held the height variance. The rezoning objector withdrew, so no Municipal Board hearing was needed; on Aug 15 council gave third reading and approved the full 120 ft.
status_detail: Approved as applied, including the 120-ft height most speakers objected to. Councillors asked for an Albert Street sidewalk discussion at a study session (no result found in this period).
figures: Height 120 ft vs 85 ft RMX limit; Credit Union building about 110 ft (transcript 2017-08-15 0:28:28).
reasons: meets-the-plan: RMX has less impact than existing C-4 regional commercial. (Michael Zwaagstra); precedent: Under C-4 the owner could build any height without a variance. (Councillor Penner); need-housing: Personal care beds and supportive housing urgently needed. (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: Rest Haven next door generates little traffic. (John Fehr)
public: One letter objecting to the rezoning (later withdrawn); one information letter on the variance. Residents G.C., C.K., T.H., W.G. and A.M. spoke; most said they accepted the rezoning but objected to the height; concerns included parking, traffic, a sidewalk on Albert, property values and privacy.
vote: R17-141 carried unanimously (minutes); third reading and variance Aug 15 moved and seconded by the two Councillors Penner, carried (Zwaagstra absent)
notes: Only the 2017-07-18 minutes exist for this period; they record R17-141 and R17-142 (V-2017-11). The variance vote on Aug 15 had a call for 'opposed' with no dissent named.

title: Church in the industrial park (88 Acres Drive) approved despite one written objection
summary: Ecclesia Fellowship Church applied (CU-2017-02) to locate in the M-1 light industrial zone on city-owned land it was buying. One written objection and one letter of support were received; no one objected at the hearing. Council approved, citing precedents for churches in that zone, then approved the $78,000 land sale.
status_detail: Approved as applied.
figures: Land sale $78,000 (transcript 0:15:39).
reasons: precedent: Council has approved churches in this zone before. (Troy Warkentin)
public: One written objection (author and grounds not read out); one letter of support.
vote: carried (call for 'opposed' made; no dissent named)
notes: The objection's content is not described in the transcript.

title: 486 Main Street 8-plex/5-plex: neighbours' concerns handled by the applicant before the hearing; approved
summary: CU-2017-07 and V-2017-16 sought multifamily in the C-2 zone with less ground-floor commercial, a repeat of a 2013 approval that had lapsed. No written correspondence was received. Three neighbours spoke: one thanked the applicant for agreeing to no windows or balconies facing her yard and a 15-ft green buffer; another asked about setbacks, drainage and a promised 8-ft fence; a third asked about sightlines on Main Street. Council approved the conditional use.
status_detail: Conditional use approved subject to a development agreement; the applicant's commitments were made directly to neighbours, not as council conditions. The variance vote is not captured in the transcript.
figures: 2-storey 8-plex, 2-storey 5-plex and 2-storey commercial building; 14.5 ft from a neighbour's line (transcript 0:29:27).
reasons: already-consulted: Applicant met neighbours and mitigated fencing, vegetation and parking. (Chris Goertzen); precedent: Same plan approved in 2013. (Troy Warkentin)
public: P.E. (thanked the applicant for privacy changes), T.G. (setback, drainage, fence height), D.P. (Main Street sightlines). No formal objections.
notes: Transcript moves to other business after the CU vote; whether V-2017-16 was voted separately is unverified.

title: Official community plan and zoning by-law review promised with public consultation
summary: With annexation expected, council applied for a provincial grant (up to 50%) to review the official community plan and zoning by-law. Mayor Goertzen said the review must include public consultation using the mechanisms of past reviews. Council later pointed objectors on Brant Street (Dec 5) and digital-sign questions (Nov 2016) to this review.
status_detail: Grant application approved; the review and its consultation fall after this period.
figures: Provincial grant up to 50% of cost (transcript 0:17:41).

title: 80 Brant Street plan change to commercial denied after neighbours objected
summary: Envision (Association for Community Living, Steinbach Branch) applied to redesignate 80 Brant Street from residential to commercial in the official community plan (By-law 2087) and rezone it to C-2 (By-law 2088) for offices. Councillors gave first reading Nov 7 saying they wanted to hear the public. At the Dec 5 hearing at least five neighbours objected: not to Envision, but to commercial creeping down the residential block, traffic and safety on Brant, and property values. Administration said there was no zoning tool to allow only Envision's use. Council denied the plan change, so the rezoning hearing was never held.
status_detail: Denied; objections changed the outcome. Council said the area should be considered in the 2018 official community plan review instead.
reasons: meets-the-plan: Long-term decision; review the whole area in the 2018 OCP review, not one property at one meeting. (Jac Siemens); precedent: Can't tie commercial designation to one user; long-term risk for the street. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Objectors K.L., A.P., B.B., R.J., a resident identified only as 'Mr. F.', and one speaker whose opening was not recorded: fear of commercial spreading along Brant, traffic and accidents near Woodhaven, property values (one cited a $30,000 drop estimate from realtors, unverified). G.C., the owner of 80 Brant, supported.
notes: The Dec 5, 2017 recording is audio-only and starts partway through the hearing, so the staff report, notice details, staff recommendation and the applicant's presentation are missing.

title: 260 Park Road West: after-the-fact paving variance approved against staff advice (split vote)
summary: A business on a gravel road asked to be excused from paving its required parking (V-2017-26), a requirement in its approved 2015 lot grading plan. There were no objectors or letters. Staff recommended denial. A majority approved it, saying paving on gravel roads makes little sense; Mayor Goertzen and Councillor Zwaagstra spoke against.
status_detail: Approved over the staff recommendation; councillors asked for a broader look at paving rules on gravel roads (no result in this period).
reasons: property-rights: Paving lots on gravel roads doesn't make sense; take the apology in good faith. (Councillor Penner)
public: No objectors; the applicant (O.K.) spoke.
vote: carried; Mayor Goertzen and Michael Zwaagstra stated they were against (full count not stated)
notes: Uncontested hearing; included because of the divided vote against staff advice.

title: Golf course land deal: request to hear from the public before deciding was defeated
summary: Council bought 40 acres from the Steinbach Fly-In Golf Club for $500,000 over 3 years and leased it back for $1 a year. Councillor Zwaagstra said that in closed meetings he had moved to have the golf club present in public and wait a couple of weeks for public feedback, and that motion was defeated 4-3; he and others said payment over 3 years avoided Municipal Board scrutiny of a debenture. Councillor Fehr replied that land deals are always negotiated in closed session. The purchase carried.
status_detail: No public input period was held before the decision; purchase and $1 lease approved Dec 5, 2017.
figures: $500,000 over 3 years; lease $1/year (transcript 1:07:14-1:07:33).
reasons: already-consulted: Land negotiations are always confidential; not prudent to discuss before a deal. (John Fehr)
vote: carried; Zwaagstra, Funk and one Councillor Penner spoke against (count not stated in open session); closed-meeting public-input motion defeated 4-3 per Zwaagstra
notes: Not a land-use hearing; included under 'having a say'. The 'stance' field here records position on public input (for = wanted public input). The 4-3 closed-meeting vote is Zwaagstra's account and can't be verified (no minutes).

title: 2018: 20 planning hearings drew no objectors
summary: Of 29 planning hearings held in 2018 (Feb 20 - Nov 20), 20 had no written objection and no objector present, according to the minutes. Most were approved unanimously. Council still changed or refused some on its own judgment: it denied the home-business part of V-2018-08 (426 Rockwood St) 4-2, limited V-2018-09 (320 Main St) to a fence around the HVAC units only, and attached a $5,200-a-year parking condition to the Calvary Chapel parking variance V-2018-21 (305 Main St) after two amendments to soften it failed 3-4.
status_detail: Hearings with no objectors: Sub 4451-2017-7942, CU-2018-01, V-2018-02, V-2018-01, V-2018-04, By-law 2094, V-2018-08, V-2018-09, CU-2018-03, V-2018-11, Sub 4451-2018-7990, CU-2018-04, V-2018-17, V-2018-18, V-2018-19, CU-2018-05 (6-1, C. Penner against), V-2018-21, V-2018-24 (6-1, C. Penner against), CU-2018-06, plus the 2018 financial plan hearing (not counted). CU-2018-01 (SCU parking lot, Reimer Ave) was adjourned on Mar 6 so the applicant could attend; no decision was found in the 2018 minutes.
figures: 29 planning hearings in 2018; 9 contested, 20 without objectors (minutes). V-2018-21 condition: annual payment of $5,200 (minutes Oct 2, 2018).
public: None objected. Sub 4451-2018-7990 (Prairie Crescent) had one item of correspondence from a resident (L.R.) whose content the minutes do not record; it is counted here as uncontested. V-2018-21 had one letter of support; the applicant said the hockey community had parking concerns.
notes: Count built from the 'Public Hearing was to consider' entries in the 2018 minutes. Jan 2018 meetings had no hearings.

title: How neighbours heard: statutory notice, applicants' own canvassing, and complaints of no early say
summary: Every hearing in the minutes opens with the City Manager reporting that 'notices pursuant to The Planning Act had been completed' (or The Municipal Act for local improvements and service plans). Beyond that, outreach depended on the applicant: the Resthaven addition mailed about 50 letters and held an open house (2018); the Maplewood applicant hand-delivered material to about 70 neighbours (2018); the 44 First St applicants said 45 properties had received notice and they contacted all 16 owner-occupants (2019). Council praised applicants who consulted and criticized those who did not. Residents complained that a 2018 notice was posted on only one street, that they had no chance to give an opinion before the Clearspring Greens pathway plan was set (2020), and that the city did not contact enVision before mailing the Acres Drive local-improvement notice (2020).
status_detail: No change to the city's notice method was found in 2018-2020; council did not discuss the notice complaints.
figures: Resthaven ~50 letters, open house attended by 4 (minutes Apr 3, 2018); 44 First St: 45 properties noticed, 16 owner-occupied (minutes July 16, 2019).
reasons: notice-meets-act: reports at each hearing that Planning Act notices were completed (Troy Warkentin); already-consulted: credits applicants who consulted neighbours; faults those who did not (CU-2019-03, By-law 2101) (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: T.B. (2018) said notice should have been posted on both streets a project faces. At the Clearspring Greens hearing D.B. said he had no opportunity to give an opinion earlier and D.J. wanted neighbourhood involvement (minutes Jan 7, 2020). enVision's board president (G.D.) said the city did not reach out before the notice was sent (minutes Dec 15, 2020).
notes: Whether 'posting' meant a sign on the property or the mailing area is not stated.

title: Funeral home at 32 PTH 52 West denied after neighbours and businesses objected over parking
summary: CU-2018-02 would have allowed a 100-seat funeral home in an existing building at 32 PTH 52 West. Five letters and seven speakers (condo owners and neighbouring businesses) objected, mainly that parking on the site was already a daily problem. Council denied the conditional use unanimously, citing the parking concerns it had heard.
status_detail: Denied unanimously (R18-070). A funeral home was approved at 40 North Gate Drive on Aug 7, 2018 (CU-2018-04) with no objectors.
figures: 5 letters, 7 speakers; 25 stalls required for 100 seats (minutes Apr 3, 2018).
public: Residents of 20 and 40 PTH 52 West (C.F., D.F., J.K. and others) and businesses including El Vecino Foods and Grand Denture Clinic objected to parking; C.F. and D.F. also cited property values.

title: Resthaven nursing home addition: front-yard variance approved over one neighbour's objection
summary: V-2018-05 sought an 11.5-ft front yard (25 ft required) at 185 Woodhaven Ave for a 142-bed personal care addition. The nursing home said it mailed about 50 letters to neighbours and held an open house on Mar 14, 2018 that 4 people attended. One neighbour (T.M.) supported the project but objected to the size of the variance along a public sidewalk.
status_detail: Approved unanimously, subject to a development agreement (R18-069).
figures: 11 ft 6 in front yard vs 25 ft required; ~50 letters mailed by applicant; open house attended by 4 (minutes Apr 3, 2018).
public: T.M. objected that an 11.5-ft setback was a significant variance and a violation of zoning standards.

title: 47-77 First Street townhouses: rezoning given second reading, front-yard variance denied, objections sent file to Municipal Board
themes: rezoning; variance; infill; municipal-board; staff-recommendation; letters
summary: By-law 2092 rezoned six First Street lots from RLD to RMD for two-storey townhouses, with V-2018-03 for a 15-ft front yard (25 ft required). One letter (M.M.) and one speaker (T.B.) objected (sewer, schools, traffic, neighbourhood change). Council gave second reading unanimously, but defeated the variance 3-4 and formally denied it 4-3 on May 15; administration had recommended denying the variance. Because objections were registered, the by-law went to a Municipal Board hearing (Aug 27, 2018). The Board approved it with extra conditions, including a back lane, and council gave third reading on Apr 16, 2019.
status_detail: Rezoning approved after the Municipal Board review with Board-imposed conditions; the front-yard variance was denied (R18-091 defeated, R18-105). Third reading R19-102 (Apr 16, 2019).
figures: 15 ft front yard requested vs 25 ft; 1 letter + 1 speaker; Municipal Board hearing Aug 27, 2018 (minutes R18-196, R19-102).
reasons: meets-the-plan: infill and density are part of the official community plan; infrastructure is the developer's cost (Mayor Chris Goertzen); staff-recommends: acknowledged administration recommended denying the variance but supported it anyway (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: M.M. (letter) objected to apartments beside her property; T.B. cited sewer backups and capacity, schools, traffic and children in the street. The applicant said he had contacted some neighbours.
vote: 2nd reading unanimous; variance approval defeated 3-4; variance denial 4-3

title: Province raises the number of objections needed to send a rezoning to the Municipal Board
summary: In 2018 even one or two objectors at second reading sent a rezoning to a Municipal Board hearing (By-laws 2092 and 2097). By mid-2019 an amendment to The Planning Act required a minimum number and share of objectors, who must also renew their objection directly to the Board. The City Manager explained this on July 2, 2019, and Councillor Zwaagstra called it 'good' because a few objectors no longer override council. From then on, third reading routinely followed second reading the same night when objections fell short (By-laws 2125, 2148, 2143).
status_detail: Provincial change, not a council decision; council welcomed it. No council resolution on it was found.
figures: 2018: 2 objectors enough for a Board hearing (transcript May 1, 2018). 2020: 4-5 objections 'not sufficient' (transcript June 16, 2020).
reasons: objections-not-planning-grounds: if objectors are not a significant number, council's decision should stand (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: The exact statutory threshold and amendment date were not stated in the meetings; check The Planning Amendment Act (2018/2019) before publishing a number.

title: Sunroom built too close to rear line at 66 Edgewood St denied after neighbours objected
summary: V-2018-06 sought after-the-fact approval of a sunroom with a 12.35-ft rear yard (25 ft required) and a shed 1.8 ft from the line. Three letters (including Poplar Estates Ltd.) and two speakers objected; the owner did not attend. Council denied the sunroom and approved the shed on condition the fence be moved onto the owner's property.
status_detail: Sunroom variance denied; shed variance approved with a fence-relocation condition (R18-108, unanimous).
figures: 12.35 ft rear yard vs 25 ft; 3 letters, 2 speakers (minutes May 15, 2018).
public: Neighbours on Alderwood Cres and Fernwood Bay (H.T., E.S., K.K., M.G.) and Poplar Estates Ltd. objected to the addition.

title: 122-124 Brandt St multi-family rezoning approved after Municipal Board hearing triggered by two objectors
summary: By-law 2097 rezoned two Brandt St lots from RLD to RMD for a multi-family building, with V-2018-07 for a 19-ft rear yard. Two residents of one household (T.B. and L.B.) objected (traffic, parking, no sidewalk, infrastructure, building line). Council gave second reading unanimously; the objections sent it to a Municipal Board hearing on Aug 8, 2018, which approved it with conditions. Council gave third reading and approved the variance on Sept 18, 2018.
status_detail: Approved; Municipal Board order (B-18006) added conditions; third reading R18-208 and variance R18-209, both unanimous.
figures: 19 ft rear yard vs 25 ft; 2 objectors (minutes June 5, 2018); Board hearing Aug 8, 2018 (R18-183).
public: T.B. cited traffic, parking, pedestrian safety (no sidewalk) and underground infrastructure; L.B. said the building would not line up with others on the street.
notes: The Board's specific conditions were not read into the record; the 2019-2020 transcripts say a Board ruling on a First Street file required a paved back lane (that ruling appears to be By-law 2092).

title: Lot split at 404 First St / Barkman Ave denied after six neighbours objected
summary: V-2018-10 and subdivision 4451-2018-8015 would have split a corner lot so the owners could build a small retirement home, with a 4,247 sq ft lot (5,500 required) and 8.1-ft rear yards. One letter and six speakers objected (lot too small, drainage, traffic and parking on Barkman, loss of trees); two said they had objected to a similar application that was denied in 2006. Staff recommended denial and council denied both unanimously.
status_detail: Variance (R18-135) and subdivision (R18-136) denied unanimously.
figures: 4,247 sq ft vs 5,500 minimum; 8.1 ft rear yard vs 25 ft; 1 letter + 6 speakers (minutes June 19, 2018).
public: Neighbours (A.G., Y.S., E.D., H.D., K.S., and E.K. for G. and A.D.) objected; A.G. and Y.S. noted a similar file was denied in 2006 after their objections.

title: 44-unit Maplewood St townhouse rezoning denied after 49 letters (84 signatures) and ten speakers
themes: rezoning; infill; letters; petition; notice; municipal-board
summary: By-law 2101 would have rezoned seven Maplewood St lots from RLD to RMD for four 11-unit townhouse buildings. The applicant said he hand-delivered information to about 70 neighbours. Residents filed 49 letters of objection with 84 signatures and ten people spoke (traffic, drainage, maintenance of the owner's existing rentals, privacy, school buses, aesthetics). One objector complained that the notice was posted only on the Maplewood side. Council denied second reading 5-1.
status_detail: Second reading denied 5-1 (R18-191; S. Penner against); the by-law died. A redesigned 72-suite plan for the same lots was approved in May-July 2020 (see 2020-maplewood-bylaw-2147).
figures: 44 units; 49 letters / 84 signatures; 10 speakers (minutes Aug 21, 2018).
reasons: meets-the-plan: Maplewood is a collector street in the community plan and multifamily already exists nearby (Susan Penner)
public: D.M. presented 49 letters (84 signatures). R.W., G.K., W.K., S.R., J.R., C.R., M.V.N., K.B., H.F. and T.B. raised traffic, drainage, upkeep of the owner's existing houses, children's safety, privacy and whether drawings were final; R.W. said she would accept duplexes. T.B. said notice should have been posted on both Maplewood and Stonebridge.

title: Five-foot side yards at 109-110 Alderwood Cres approved 6-1 over a fire-safety letter
summary: V-2018-22 sought 5-ft east side yards (8 ft required) on two lots. One neighbour (E.S.) wrote that closer houses could let fire spread more quickly. Council approved, on condition that only single-family homes be built.
status_detail: Approved 6-1 (R18-210; Fehr against) with a single-family-only condition; the minutes do not link the condition to the objection.
figures: 5 ft vs 8 ft side yard; 1 letter (minutes Sept 18, 2018).
public: E.S. (letter) objected that fire could spread more quickly between houses.

title: Harmony Lane public reserve closed 4-3 despite two neighbours who bought for the green space
themes: subdivision; rezoning; variance; tabled; municipal-board; process
summary: By-law 2102 closed part of a public reserve so a new owner could reconfigure lots (with rezoning By-law 2103 and variance V-2018-25). Two Chrysler Gate residents objected that they would lose direct access to green space that had influenced their purchase. The mayor adjourned the hearing, then reopened it later the same evening after the City Manager explained the options; council gave second reading 4-3. The new council deferred third reading on Nov 20 and gave it on Dec 4, 2018.
status_detail: Second reading 4-3 (R18-249; Siemens, Funk, Fehr against); third reading R18-279 unanimous after deferral (R18-255); By-law 2103 third reading Jan 15, 2019 (R19-007); variance approved Jan 15, 2019 (R19-008).
figures: 2 objectors, no written objections (minutes Oct 16, 2018).
reasons: precedent: fewer future variances is better planning (Michael Zwaagstra); notice-meets-act: a reserve closing needs the minister's approval; he found no Municipal Board hearing route for objectors (Troy Warkentin)
public: G.D. and K.A. objected to losing direct access to the green space; G.D. said a sales agent had discussed the reserve with him.

title: Curbside garbage fee by-law passed after two residents asked for pay-by-volume
summary: Special Service Plan By-law 2111 set residential garbage fees ($137 in 2019, $141 in 2020, $145 in 2021). Two letters were received; two residents objected that everyone pays the same regardless of how much garbage they put out, and a resident of the newly annexed area asked for a refund of fees charged before pickup began. Council referred the refund request to the City Manager and gave second reading unanimously.
status_detail: Second reading Dec 4, 2018 (R18-269); Municipal Board approved; third reading Feb 5, 2019 (R19-028). The refund request was referred to administration; no outcome recorded.
figures: $137 / $141 / $145 per unit per year 2019-2021 (minutes Dec 4, 2018).
public: M.G. and A.D. asked for volume-based charges; E.P. asked for a refund for Jan-Aug 2018.

title: 2019: 15 planning hearings drew no objectors
summary: Of 24 planning hearings in 2019, 15 had no objector according to the minutes. Most passed unanimously. Council refused the street-edge landscaping waiver V-2019-01 (29 Cambridge Way) 5-2 although nobody objected, and cut a parking waiver (V-2019-16, 306 Main St) to a reduction of seven stalls on staff's advice after a neighbouring owner asked questions.
status_detail: No-objector hearings: V-2019-01 (denied 5-2), V-2019-02, V-2019-05, V-2019-06, Sub 4451-2018-8099, CU-2019-01, V-2019-09, CU-2019-02, V-2019-16, V-2019-17, CU-2019-04, By-law 2126, Sub 4451-2019-8186, By-law 2129 (lane closing, Dec 3), V-2019-29. Also local improvement By-law 2131 (Kroeker Ave), no objections.
figures: 24 planning hearings in 2019; 9 contested (minutes).

title: Hospital Street lots rezoned for Southern Health after two neighbours raised drainage and safety
summary: By-law 2109 rezoned 409-421 Hospital St from RLD to Educational/Institutional for Southern Health. Two neighbours raised drainage, privacy, through-access, fencing and teenagers using the lot; the applicant said a culvert would handle drainage. Council gave second and third readings unanimously.
status_detail: Approved, subject to consolidation of the lots (R19-045, R19-046).
public: O.M. and C.K. raised concerns; neither is recorded as formally objecting.
notes: Minutes: R19-045 Zwaagstra / S. Penner; R19-046 D. Penner / J. Hiebert. (The motions CSV mis-parses the R19-045 mover.) No transcript for Mar 5, 2019.

title: Resthaven parking-lot variance approved; neighbour's request for a privacy fence not added
summary: V-2019-12 let a parking lot be built at 159 Woodhaven Ave before the main building. A neighbour (D.F.) whose yard backs onto the site asked for a privacy fence; the applicant said parking would be only on the Woodhaven side. Approved unanimously with a shared driveway and parking agreement.
status_detail: Approved (R19-107) subject to shared driveway, parking and cross-access agreement; no fence condition.
public: D.F. raised privacy and asked for a fence.

title: Nine-unit building at 126 Maplewood St approved over a 56-name petition
summary: By-law 2120 rezoned 126 Maplewood St to RMD for a nine-unit building, with V-2019-11 for a 56-ft site width (75 required). A 56-name petition, one letter and five speakers objected (traffic, parking, renters, upkeep, property values, the large variance); one resident spoke in support. Council gave second reading unanimously. No objector renewed the objection to the Municipal Board, so third reading and the variance passed on July 2, 2019.
status_detail: Second reading R19-118 (May 21); third reading R19-147 and variance R19-148 (July 2), all unanimous.
figures: 9 units; 56-name petition; 56 ft vs 75 ft site width (minutes May 21, 2019).
reasons: meets-the-plan: nine units is small; many apartments already nearby; unique deep lot (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: traffic on Maplewood is largely through-traffic; denying would not solve it (Jac Siemens)
public: R.W. submitted the 56-name petition; I.F., K.F., J.R. and W.K. objected; A.D. supported the rezoning.

title: Eight-suite apartment at 216 Hanover St denied: neighbours' 54-name petition and no consultation
summary: CU-2019-03 and V-2019-13 would have allowed an eight-suite apartment with no main-floor commercial space in the C1 zone at 216 Hanover St. Three letters, a 54-name petition and two speakers objected (trees, drainage, density, character), and one said the applicant had not consulted neighbours. Council denied both unanimously; several members said the lack of consultation decided it and invited a better-consulted plan.
status_detail: Conditional use (R19-140) and variance (R19-141) denied unanimously; the City Manager said the topic could not return for one year.
figures: 8 suites; 3 letters, 54-name petition, 2 speakers (minutes July 2, 2019).
public: J.D. presented the 54-name petition (trees, drainage, too much building); J.R. said density did not suit the street and the applicant did not consult neighbours; T.H., K.H. and M.H. wrote objecting.

title: Eight-unit building at 44 First St approved 4-3 over neighbours' precedent concerns
themes: rezoning; variance; infill; letters; municipal-board; precedent
summary: By-law 2125 rezoned 44 First St (south side) from RLD to RMD for an eight-unit building, with V-2019-18 for a 70-ft frontage (75 required). Two letters and six speakers objected (precedent for the south side of First St, size, privacy, traffic, the variance). A motion to deny failed 3-4 and second reading passed 4-3. There were not enough objections to require a Municipal Board hearing, so third reading passed 4-3 on Aug 20 and the variance 5-2.
figures: 8 units; 70 ft vs 75 ft frontage; 2 letters + 6 speakers; 45 properties received notice, 16 owner-occupied (minutes July 16, 2019).
reasons: meets-the-plan: the plan designates the area residential; RMD is still residential (Michael Zwaagstra); already-consulted: the developer went to the neighbourhood before coming to council (Mayor Earl Funk); objections-not-planning-grounds: the few people present may not represent the whole area (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: J.B., T.B., M.J. (owner of nearby properties), J.G. and developer L.W. (who is building across the street) objected; the owners of 40 First St wrote objecting. T.B. commended the applicants for speaking to neighbours.

title: Clearspring Greens pathway: residents asked for it, then objected to paying for it; plan cut back
summary: About 100 Clearspring Greens residents asked council for a safe pathway in July 2019. Council proposed Local Improvement Plan 2020-02: an 850-m lit, fenced asphalt path costing $625,000, charged to 146 properties at $4,280.82 each (or $1,044.05 a year for 5 years), with the city buying a lot for access. At the Jan 7, 2020 hearing 16 households wrote and about 20 residents objected (cost, route, lighting, no say beforehand). Council gave first and second reading 5-2 after defeating a cheaper limestone, no-lighting amendment 2-5. On Jan 21, council voted 6-1 to have the city pay for the lighting. 32 objections were filed; staff said 10% of owners renewing to the Municipal Board would force a Board hearing.
status_detail: Lighting cost moved to the city (R20-012). The 2020 project never received authority to proceed (tender held back Apr 7, 2020). On Jan 5, 2021 council cancelled the plan as objections were 'so significant', and a revised plan (Feb 16, 2021 transcript) capped the charge at 50% of cost, max $1,610 per parcel.
figures: $625,000; 146 parcels; $4,280.82 up front or $1,044.05/yr x 5 (minutes Jan 7, 2020); 32 objections (transcript Jan 21, 2020); revised cap $1,610 (transcript Feb 16, 2021).
reasons: already-consulted: the neighbourhood requested the project; council acted on that request (Damian Penner); precedent: local improvements are paid by the benefiting area; won't raise everyone else's share (Michael Zwaagstra); notice-meets-act: an open community session would not produce consensus (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: S.J., S.P., G.P., D.J., B.F., D.B., L.C., S.H., E.F., L.L., D.B., R.M., E.F., J.B., T.B., J.A., C.D., A.D., J.W. and S.F. objected (cost, route, lighting, fence, property value); D.B. said he had no chance to give an opinion beforehand; another resident would accept paying a quarter of the charge.

title: One-foot side yard for a garage at 28 Alexander Way denied after a neighbour objected
summary: V-2019-19 sought a 1-ft side yard (4 ft required) for a garage. One resident (M.G.) objected over drainage and fire safety. A motion to approve a 2-ft compromise found no seconder, and council denied the variance 5-1.
status_detail: Denied 5-1 (R19-158; Siemens against).
public: M.G. objected (drainage, fire safety close to the neighbouring house).

title: Front-yard fence at 2 Granite Park Blvd approved with height limits after a visibility objection
summary: V-2019-20 sought a 4-ft front-yard fence (3 ft allowed). One neighbour wrote objecting over reduced visibility. Council approved with conditions: posts no higher than 4 ft and rails no higher than 3 ft.
status_detail: Approved with height conditions (R19-182, unanimous).
public: P.S. (letter) objected over visibility.

title: Eight high-density lots and Woodhaven Ave widening approved over two neighbours' concerns
summary: Subdivision 4451-2019-8174 created eight RHD lots and widened Woodhaven Ave. One letter and two neighbours raised neighbourhood change, child safety and privacy; the applicant noted a 45-ft easement and that the land had been zoned for apartments since 1990. Approved unanimously.
status_detail: Approved (R19-201) subject to a development agreement and road-closing By-law 2129.
public: C.S. and D.K. raised concerns; P. and J.T. wrote.
notes: No transcript for Oct 15, 2019 (not in the transcript set); minutes only.

title: 41 Brandt St: rear-yard variance approved but parking cut denied after neighbouring owners objected
summary: V-2019-26 sought a 4-ft rear yard (20 ft required) and 19 parking stalls instead of 28. A lawyer for six nearby properties, a dental clinic and two other neighbours objected to the parking reduction (safety, visibility, no street parking, drainage), not the rear yard. Council approved the rear yard and denied the parking reduction unanimously.
status_detail: Split decision R19-212 (unanimous): rear yard approved, parking reduction denied.
figures: 19 vs 28 stalls; 4 ft vs 20 ft rear yard (minutes Nov 5, 2019).
public: Loewen Henderson Banman Legault LLP for six properties, Choice Dental Care, K.P. and Century 21 (D.R.) objected to the reduced parking.
notes: No transcript for Nov 5, 2019; minutes only.

title: 2020: 26 planning hearings drew no objectors, held in chambers under COVID rules
summary: Of 34 planning hearings in 2020 (including two on May 19, for which minutes are missing), 26 had no objector. Council refused one anyway: V-2020-24 (waiving street-edge landscaping at 435 PTH 12 N) was denied 4-3. From March 2020 meetings were livestreamed and hearings continued in the council chamber, with the chair waiting while speakers were brought into the room one at a time.
figures: 34 planning hearings in 2020; 8 contested (minutes; transcript for May 19).
notes: The COVID procedure is inferred from the recordings (waiting for speakers to be brought in); no written procedure was found in the minutes.

title: Parkhill phase 2 rezoning and subdivision approved; one rural neighbour objected over road traffic
summary: By-law 2143 repealed a secondary plan, By-law 2140 rezoned land and subdivision 4451-2019-8250 created 60 lots off McKenzie Ave. One Bush Farm Road resident objected to all three over traffic and asked whether the road would be hard-surfaced. With only one objection there was no Municipal Board referral; council gave second and third readings and approved the subdivision unanimously.
status_detail: Approved: R20-046, R20-047, R20-050 (unanimous).
public: G.H. objected (traffic on Bush Farm Road).

title: Maplewood St lots denied in 2018 rezoned in 2020 after a redesigned, consulted plan
summary: By-law 2147 rezoned 135-191 Maplewood St, the same lots refused in 2018 (By-law 2101), for a redesigned 72-suite, two-storey project. The new applicant consulted the neighbourhood and city staff. One neighbour raised drainage; a councillor asked for a one-way access. Council gave second reading on May 19 and third reading on July 7, 2020, after administration worked further with the applicant.
status_detail: Second reading carried May 19 (transcript; minutes missing); third reading unanimous July 7, 2020 subject to a development agreement.
figures: 72 suites (transcript May 19, 2020).
reasons: already-consulted: applicant did more work than any previous developer; concerns are drainage, which engineers will handle (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: K.B. raised drainage on Home St; no formal objectors are recorded.
notes: Mover/seconder from the transcript (0:42:25-0:42:31): Siemens moved, 'Councillor Switzer' (Zwaagstra) seconded.

title: Oversized shed at 411 Rockwood St approved despite neighbours' written complaints
summary: V-2020-09 sought an accessory building 200 sq ft larger than the 1,000 sq ft allowed in the rural residential zone. Council had written complaints about RVs and trailers on the yard; the owner said he was not running a business and the building would let him store a motorhome inside. Councillor Siemens moved approval, saying the building might clean up the yard.
status_detail: Approved (transcript); the May 19, 2020 minutes are not in the archive.
public: Neighbours wrote complaining about vehicles and trailers stored on the property (number not stated).

title: Council objects to Bill 48 letting developers appeal its land-use decisions
summary: The province's Bill 48 (Planning Amendment and City of Winnipeg Charter Amendment Act) proposed appeals to the Municipal Board for applicants and new planning regions. The City Manager reported concerns. Council voted unanimously to send them, arguing that developer appeals could overturn decisions made after listening to neighbours. Councillor Siemens cited the Board's earlier ruling that forced a back lane on a First Street development.
status_detail: City Manager directed to forward concerns (R20-120, unanimous). The bill's fate was outside council's control.

title: Ten-unit building at 78 First St approved the same night over four objectors
summary: By-law 2148 rezoned 78 First St from RLD to RMD for a second 10-unit building beside the owner's first. One letter of concern and four speakers objected (traffic and congestion on First St, safety walking to the park, amount of development, affordability; one suggested a side-by-side). The applicant said he had written to neighbours. Council gave second reading unanimously and, with only four or five objections, third reading the same night.
status_detail: Second (R20-127) and third (R20-128) readings unanimous, subject to a development agreement.
figures: 10 units; 4 objectors + 1 email; 82 multifamily units already approved on First St in recent years (transcript June 16, 2020).
reasons: traffic-manageable: 9-10 more vehicles a day is small (Michael Zwaagstra); need-housing: units rented before completion show demand; older lots are costly to redevelop (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: F.D., I.T., C.S. and L.R. objected; L.S. wrote with concerns.

title: Six-plex at 14 Ellice Ave denied after a petition and six objecting neighbours
summary: By-law 2152 and V-2020-17 would have allowed a six-unit development on a narrow lot at 14 Ellice Ave. The applicants had canvassed neighbours with two designs. A petition, letters and six speakers objected (setbacks, privacy, drainage, parking, traffic, green space, property values). Council denied second reading unanimously; several members said RMD zoning could work but six units was too aggressive for the lot, and the mayor invited a reworked plan.
status_detail: Second reading denied unanimously (R20-156); the variance was not considered.
figures: 6 units; 71.5 ft vs 75 ft site width; 1 petition + written objections + 6 speakers (minutes Aug 18, 2020).
public: B.T., G.P., E.W., L.G., P.S. and M.G. objected; a petition was filed.

title: COVID visitation shelter at 185 Woodhaven Ave approved after a neighbour's questions
summary: CU-2020-07 allowed a moved-in building as a COVID visitation shelter at Resthaven. A neighbour across the street (T.M.) asked about its location, how long it would stay and shipping-container rules, and expressed concern about execution. Approved unanimously.
status_detail: Approved (R20-196).
public: T.M. asked questions and expressed concern.

title: Five-foot front-yard fence at 1 Rosewood Pl approved on compassionate grounds over neighbours' petition
summary: V-2020-27 sought to keep a 5-ft front-yard chain-link fence (3 ft allowed) built to keep two children with disabilities from running into the street. Five letters and a petition from five households objected (eyesore, property values, precedent, the fence was built illegally); two letters and a petition from six Rosewood Place households supported it. Council approved 4-1, with members calling it a unique, compassionate case and not a precedent.
status_detail: Approved 4-1 (R20-216; J. Hiebert against). Councillor S. Penner noted the applicant said she would remove the fence when she moves.
figures: 5 ft vs 3 ft; 5 letters + 5-household petition against; 2 letters + 6-household petition for (minutes Nov 3, 2020).
reasons: precedent: each variance is unique; approving this one sets no precedent (Susan Penner)
public: M.C. and D.H. spoke against; letters from J.&B.G., A.D., N.R., D.&M.H., M.&D.C. Neighbours on Rosewood Place petitioned in support.
notes: The minutes record the resolution as approving 'V-2020-28' although the hearing was V-2020-27.

title: Woodhaven Ave down-zoning approved; neighbours' 12-of-15 petition for a fence not made a condition
summary: By-law 2159 rezoned 224-232 Woodhaven Ave from RHD to RMD (lower density). A resident (C.S.) brought a petition signed by 12 of the 15 properties backing onto the site, asking that a wooden privacy fence be required to stop foot traffic; she said it was a request, not an objection. The mayor said fences are generally not required on new development, as opposed to infill. Approved unanimously without a fence condition.
status_detail: Second and third readings unanimous (R20-217, R20-218), subject to a development agreement; no fence condition recorded.
figures: Petition: 12 of 15 backing properties (minutes Nov 3, 2020); 45-ft public reserve buffer.
reasons: meets-the-plan: lower density than allowed; 45-ft buffer; fence conditions are for infill, not new construction (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: C.S. presented the 12-of-15 petition requesting a fence.

title: Acres Drive local improvement proceeds over enVision's 114-signature objection
summary: Local Improvement Plan 2021-02 extends Acres Drive and its water main, charging fronting properties by frontage. enVision (a community-living charity) objected by letter, through its lawyer and with a 114-signature petition, saying it would not benefit, would have to cut services, and that the city did not contact it before mailing the notice. Council gave first reading 5-1.
status_detail: First reading 5-1 (R20-251; Siemens against). The 2021 financial plan lists Acres Drive debt, so the project appears to have proceeded; later readings were outside this period.
reasons: precedent: local improvements are always charged on frontage; exempting a non-profit would set a precedent (Michael Zwaagstra); meets-the-plan: levies are on land, not use; the by-law requires it (Susan Penner)
public: enVision (board president G.D. and J.D.) objected; its lawyer wrote; 114-signature petition.

title: Brandt Street water and sewer renewal local improvement: one letter against, one for
summary: Local Improvement Plan 2021-01 renews water and sewer on Brandt St, recovering debt through a utility levy. One household wrote in support and one objected. First and second readings passed unanimously.
status_detail: First and second readings unanimous (R20-252, R20-253).
figures: $2.415M total, $1.25M debt (transcript Dec 15, 2020).
public: L.L. and A.H. wrote in support; E. and A.M. wrote objecting.

title: Clearspring Greens pathway levy cancelled after 78 objections, then re-done at about half the cost
summary: A local improvement levy for a pathway to Clearspring Greens (By-law 2132, given second reading in Jan 2020) drew 78 formal objections from 146 parcels, enough to send it to the Municipal Board. On Jan 5, 2021 council, on Councillor Susan Penner's motion, cancelled it and ordered a new plan without lighting and with the city paying half, capping each parcel at $1,610. The new plan (By-law 2168) drew 7 letters of objection and 1 in support; the one objector who came to the Feb 16 hearing withdrew his objection, and council approved it unanimously.
status_detail: Objections changed the outcome: the original plan was cancelled (R21-011) and given a formal third-reading defeat (R21-031); the cheaper plan passed second reading Feb 16 and third reading Apr 20, 2021 (R21-076). The pathway was built in 2021; the Municipal Board approved the $136,850 debenture and council gave it third reading Feb 15, 2022.
figures: 78 objections of 146 parcels; Municipal Board hearing threshold for a local improvement 'at least 25 or 10%' (City Manager, transcript Jan 5, 2021 0:33:35); per-parcel cost about $4,200 originally, about $2,850 after an earlier amendment, now max $1,610 (transcript 0:34:03); project about $650,000, borrowing $233,450 (transcript Feb 16, 2021 0:09:21); 7 objections and 1 support letter (minutes Feb 16, 2021); debenture $136,850 (transcript Feb 15, 2022 0:36:18).
public: Residents had packed the 2020 hearing. In 2021 seven households wrote objecting and one wrote in support. T.B., the only objector present on Feb 16, 2021, asked why the project was back after 'a clear objection from the taxpayers last time'; told that only seven had objected this time, he withdrew his objection.
notes: Local improvement hearings fall under The Municipal Act, not The Planning Act; included because the formal objection count decided the outcome. Mayor at the hearing said 7 objections; S. Penner said 6 after T.B. withdrew.

title: 2021: 15 planning applications with no objectors, all approved
summary: Fifteen planning applications in 2021 had no objection on file and nobody speaking against: V-2020-30, V-2021-01, V-2021-02, CU-2021-01 (dog park), V-2021-03, V-2021-07, V-2021-10 (a support letter), By-law 2175 (advertising signs in M1), CU-2021-02, V-2021-15, By-law 2184 with subdivision 8466, V-2021-16, V-2021-18 (letters supplied by the applicant), V-2021-19 and CU-2021-04 (fire training building). All were approved, some with conditions (e.g. V-2021-03 old buildings removed; V-2021-19 parking only for the existing building). The 2021 financial plan hearing (Apr 6) also drew nobody.
status_detail: All approved; the only 2021 planning denials were V-2021-06 (one objecting neighbour) and the refusal to give By-law 2170 first reading.
figures: Counted from minutes and output/steinbach_council_motions.csv (public_hearing_motion = Yes).
public: None.
notes: The minutes are the source; Jul 6, 2021 (V-2021-15) has no video. By-law 2184 and subdivision 8466 are counted as one application.

title: Side-yard variance at 55 Coral Crescent denied 6-1 after a neighbour objected
summary: An owner built an attached addition (instead of the permitted detached shed) 1.9 feet from the side lot line where 4 feet is required, then applied for a variance (V-2021-06). One letter was on file and the City Manager recommended denial, citing a 2018 precedent. Council denied it.
status_detail: Denied 6-1 (R21-063), Councillor Siemens against; he would have preferred approval with a substantial fine.
figures: 1.9 ft setback vs 4 ft required (minutes Apr 6, 2021); one letter on file.
public: The neighbour's letter opposed the addition, which they said encroached on their yard (as summarized by Councillor D. Penner). No one spoke at the hearing.
notes: The objection contributed, but staff had already recommended denial; the outcome cannot be credited to the objection alone.

title: Formal objections and the Municipal Board: two by-laws referred, two others fall short
summary: Formal objections after second reading could send a by-law to the Manitoba Municipal Board. In this period that happened twice: the Acres Drive local improvement (By-law 2161, one objection; Board hearing Sep 9, 2021; approved with an amendment; third reading Feb 15, 2022) and the Wyndham Estate rezoning (By-law 2179; Board hearing Mar 2022; no conditions). Staff found too few objections to refer 115 First Street (2 objections) and 14 Ellice Ave. The McKenzie Ave fourplex (2217) was referred in 2023. Staff told council that any eligible voter may object, not only owners who were mailed notice.
status_detail: Neither Board review changed a planning result; the Acres Drive levy was amended by Board order. Council sent delegates to both hearings (R21-192, R22-057).
figures: Local improvement threshold 'at least 25 or 10%' of potential taxpayers (City Manager, Jan 5, 2021); Acres Drive borrowing up to $3.1M (transcript Feb 15, 2022 0:33:08).
public: Wyndham Estate residents used a petition; it had to be resubmitted to meet The Municipal Act.
notes: The provincial objection threshold for zoning by-laws then in force (25) is stated in the existing 2022-2026 report; it was not stated in these meetings.

title: Council refuses first reading of a church-school rezoning, so no public hearing is held
summary: By-law 2170 would have rezoned 55 Life Sciences Parkway, a church in the industrial park, from M1 to Educational/Institutional for a school. Staff recommended denying first reading. Councillors Susan Penner and Jac Siemens wanted to give first reading so neighbours and businesses could be heard at a hearing; the majority said the planning answer would not change and refused it, which ended the application without a hearing.
status_detail: First reading defeated 2-5 (R21-090); denial of first reading carried 5-2 (R21-091). Elsewhere in 2021 members described first reading as the step that lets a hearing 'hear what the neighborhood has to say' (e.g. By-law 2182, Aug 3, 2021); this was the one rezoning in the period stopped before notice went out.
reasons: staff-recommends: a school in an industrial park fails on planning grounds, so a hearing would give the same answer (Michael Zwaagstra); meets-the-plan: zoning is permanent; industrial infrastructure (no walking paths, heavy traffic) does not suit a school (Damian Penner)
public: No hearing was held, so neighbours and nearby businesses were not asked.
vote: R21-090 defeated 2-5 (for: S. Penner, Siemens); R21-091 carried 5-2 (against: S. Penner, Siemens)
notes: The 2021-08-03 first-reading comments (By-law 2182) come from unmapped speakers and are summarized, not quoted.

title: Zero front setback at 5 Loewen Blvd approved 6-1 over a neighbouring clinic owner's objection
summary: V-2021-11 let a two-storey office/commercial building sit at a 0-foot front setback where 25 feet is required. The owner of the neighbouring clinic, T.K., objected over sight lines, pedestrian and cyclist safety, parking and turning room, and access for his own future expansion. The mayor cut off questions about access agreements as off-topic. Council approved on staff's recommendation.
status_detail: Approved as applied 6-1 (R21-114); Councillor Jake Hiebert, who raised sight-line concerns, voted against.
figures: 0 ft vs 25 ft front setback (minutes Jun 1, 2021).
reasons: staff-recommends: professional staff flagged no safety concerns (Michael Zwaagstra); meets-the-plan: C-2 lots across the street already allow 0 ft setbacks (Adam Thiessen)
public: T.K., a neighbouring business owner, objected in person (safety, sight lines, traffic, access). The mayor told him that access arrangements were between the two owners and he was 'wasting council time'.
notes: Diarization merges several voices in this meeting; only the chair and mover are quoted at high confidence.

title: 107 First Street rezoned for 18 units despite one written objection
summary: By-law 2174 rezoned 107 First Street from RLD to RMD for 18 two-storey units. One neighbouring household wrote objecting; nobody spoke. Council gave second and third reading the same night.
status_detail: Second and third reading unanimous (R21-128, R21-129), subject to a development agreement.
figures: 18 units (minutes Jun 15, 2021).
reasons: need-housing: redevelopment of large old lots is only economic at medium density; fits a street already largely multi-family (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: One household on First Street objected in writing (grounds not recorded in the minutes).

title: Assisted-living conditional use on Beaver Crescent approved with two letters of concern on file
summary: CU-2021-03 allowed two 10-unit assisted-living buildings on four lots at 11-17 Beaver Crescent. Two neighbouring households wrote with concerns; nobody spoke. Council approved subject to a development agreement.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R21-141), subject to a development agreement.
figures: two buildings of 10 units (minutes Jul 6, 2021).
public: Two households (Evergreen Ave and Beaver Cres) wrote voicing concerns; content not recorded.
notes: No video: the Jul 6, 2021 recording failed to download, so this comes from the minutes only.

title: Park Road West plan change: a neighbouring owner's request for a road link is taken up by the developer
summary: OCP amendment By-law 2183 and rezoning/subdivision By-law 2184 opened a 68-acre neighbourhood west of Clearspring Centre. An architect for the property to the north asked that a planned cul-de-sac become a road connection; the developer said it was flexible. No objections were filed.
status_detail: OCP second reading Aug 17 (R21-173) and third reading Nov 2, 2021 (R21-234); subdivision approved Aug 17 and re-approved as revised Dec 21, 2021 (R21-271). All unanimous.
figures: about 68 acres (minutes Aug 17, 2021).
public: A neighbouring landowner's representative asked questions (road connection); not an objection.
mover: Michael Zwaagstra; Damian Penner; Susan Penner
notes: Counted as a hearing with questions only, not a contested one.

title: Final Hampton Village phase on Wyndham Estate Drive approved over a 58-name petition; objectors force a Municipal Board hearing
summary: By-law 2179 and a subdivision created 33 single-family lots at the end of Wyndham Estate Drive. Eight households wrote and a 58-name petition was filed; four residents spoke about children walking to the bus on a street with no sidewalk, construction traffic and parking, speeding, and one access for about 128 lots (staff policy is 120). Council gave second reading unanimously but held third reading because the objections could trigger a Municipal Board hearing. The petition was first ruled incomplete under The Municipal Act and was resubmitted.
status_detail: The Municipal Board heard the objections on Mar 16-17, 2022 and imposed no conditions; council gave third reading unanimously on May 17, 2022 (R22-129). Sidewalks on part of Wyndham, already in the 2022 budget, were included in the 2022 capital works contract awarded Mar 1, 2022; staff said the rest of Wyndham was not yet scheduled.
figures: 33 lots; more than 120 lots on one access (staff, transcript 0:42:04); 8 letters and a 58-name petition (minutes Aug 17, 2021).
reasons: meets-the-plan: final phase of a concept plan approved about 15 years earlier; no special favour to the developer (Michael Zwaagstra); need-housing: low lot inventory; keep homes affordable for 'our kids and grandkids' (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: construction is temporary; report speeding to police (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: R.C., A.B., E.B. and K.R. spoke; eight households wrote. They asked for a temporary construction road, sidewalks, and holding off until infrastructure was in place. A.B. later resubmitted the petition so it was valid under The Municipal Act.
notes: Minutes record four residents speaking (R.C. twice). Petition count (58 names) is from the minutes; signatures were not verified.

title: 115 First Street rezoned 6-1 over two in-person objections; motion to deny gets no seconder
summary: By-law 2182 added 115 First Street to the neighbouring 107 First Street project (12 more units). Two people objected in person: W.N., a nearby building owner, asked for a traffic study and more parking; S.C. raised traffic, trees and green space and said few people had seen the notice. Councillor Jake Hiebert moved to deny but found no seconder. Staff said two registered objections were not enough for a Municipal Board hearing, so third reading followed the same night.
status_detail: Second and third reading 6-1 (R21-187, R21-188), Jake Hiebert against. Several members said a traffic study for First Street should come with the next development; the annual October traffic count was cited instead.
figures: 12 additional units on top of 18 already approved (minutes Sep 7, 2021); 2 registered objections (City Manager, transcript 0:41:17).
reasons: traffic-manageable: about 12 more cars is a tiny fraction of First Street traffic (Michael Zwaagstra); need-housing: consolidated lots make better developments; higher density is better environmentally (Michael Zwaagstra); property-rights: green space is not an option on private land (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: W.N. (a neighbouring property owner and developer) and S.C. objected in person. S.C. said 'not many people saw the notice'.
notes: S.C. said she read the notice 'because I walk through there all the time'; it is unclear whether a notice was posted on site.

title: Ellice Avenue fourplex approved after the developer scaled back a plan denied in 2020
themes: rezoning; variance; infill; petition; letters; municipal-board
summary: By-law 2190 rezoned 14 Ellice Avenue to RMD for a fourplex that looks like a duplex. A six-unit version had been denied after neighbours objected in August 2020; the applicant came back with four units, bigger rear and side yards, two stalls per unit, no side windows or balconies. Neighbours still objected (four letters and a 21-signature petition from 18 properties; two spoke), mainly about precedent, a front parking lot and garbage location. Council approved and staff later found too few valid objections for a Municipal Board referral.
status_detail: Second reading unanimous Oct 19 (R21-221); third reading and the site-width variance unanimous Dec 21, 2021 (R21-272, R21-273) after staff found 'insufficient objections' for a Board referral. The 2020 objections had already cut the project from 6 to 4 units.
figures: 4 units (6 in 2020); rear yard 62 ft; 2 stalls per unit (applicant, transcript 0:24:12); petition of 21 signatures from 18 properties (minutes Oct 19, 2021); site width 71.5 ft vs 75 ft.
reasons: already-consulted: developer listened to the neighbourhood and addressed the 2020 objections (Michael Zwaagstra); precedent: council decides the plan in front of it, not possible future ones (Earl Funk)
public: E.W. (precedent; parking lot in the front yard) and B.C. (quiet street, garbage location, front parking lot) spoke against; four households wrote and 18 properties signed the petition. One councillor asked whether objections from Autumnwood Drive, outside the immediate area, were valid.
notes: The 2020 denial is outside this period; see the 2020 file.

title: Harmony Lane phase 11 rezoning and subdivision approved; one neighbour's drainage request left to engineers
summary: By-law 2189, subdivision 4451-2021-8494 and variance V-2021-21 created 37 estate lots off Harmony Lane. One neighbouring household wrote about drainage and asked for a concrete-bottom swale; the developer's agent said they were working with the city's engineers and would meet city requirements.
status_detail: Second and third reading, subdivision and variance approved unanimously (R21-217 to R21-220); the swale was not made a condition in the resolutions.
figures: 37 lots (minutes Oct 19, 2021).
reasons: staff-recommends: drainage handled through engineering review and development agreement (council)
public: One household on Hespeler St S wrote with drainage concerns.
mover: Michael Zwaagstra; Susan Penner; Jac Siemens
seconder: Susan Penner; Jake Hiebert; Bill Hiebert

title: Oversized apartment sign at 4 Brighton Lane approved; the one letter opposing it is not discussed
summary: V-2021-22 allowed a 114 sq ft, 9'3" freestanding sign in a high-density residential zone (limits 48 sq ft and 8 ft). One neighbour wrote opposing it; nobody spoke. The debate did not mention the letter.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R21-233).
figures: 114 sq ft vs 48 sq ft; 9'3" vs 8 ft (minutes Nov 16, 2021).
reasons: staff-recommends: large development; staff recommend approval (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: One neighbour on Reimer Ave wrote opposing the variance.

title: Four-storey height variance at 71 Chrysler Gate approved over a neighbour's privacy and safety concerns
summary: V-2021-25 allowed two RMD buildings with basement suites to count as four storeys where three are permitted. One letter was on file and E.W., whose back yard faces the site, raised privacy and a busy three-way stop used by school traffic. The developer offered to consider a fence. Council approved, noting the building would be no taller than an allowed three-storey one.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R21-252) without conditions; Councillor Zwaagstra said he and the mayor would raise the intersection at the RCMP advisory meeting.
figures: 4 storeys vs 3; 16 units in two buildings (minutes Dec 7, 2021).
reasons: objections-not-planning-grounds: the variance does not change height, so it has no privacy impact (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: intersection safety is an enforcement issue for the RCMP (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: E.W. (with his spouse) spoke on privacy and a dangerous intersection; one letter on file.

title: Event centre borrowing approved with seven written objections and nobody speaking
summary: Local improvement By-law 2186 authorized $7.5 million of borrowing, repaid by a city-wide levy (about 1.53 mills for five years), toward the $42.5 million Southeast Event Centre. Seven letters of objection were filed, including from Steinbach Housing and the Haven Group; no one came to speak. A councillor noted an open house Q&A on the project the day before. Council approved first and second reading.
status_detail: Second reading Dec 7, 2021 (R21-249); third reading Apr 19, 2022 (R22-100). Unanimous. The objections were not discussed in debate.
figures: $42.5M project, $7.5M borrowing, about 1.53 mills or about $138/yr on a $200,000 home (City Manager, transcript 0:06:16); 7 letters of objection (minutes Dec 7, 2021).
reasons: already-consulted: the hearing concerned only the borrowing; the project had been decided earlier (council)
public: Seven written objections (five households, Steinbach Housing and the Haven Group). Nobody attended.
notes: A councillor mentioned an open house Q&A on the event centre held the day before (Dec 6, 2021); speaker not identified.

title: Loewen Blvd / PTH 12 intersection levy: a neighbouring owner's design concerns ruled outside the hearing
