summary: Local improvement By-law 2187 financed rebuilding the Loewen Boulevard / PTH 12 North intersection. One letter was filed and K.P., speaking for his father's property at the corner, raised a turning-lane bottleneck, median access and use of private land. The mayor told him the hearing was about the debt, not the design; he did not object to the borrowing.
status_detail: First and second reading Dec 7, 2021 (R21-250, R21-251); third reading Mar 15, 2022 (R22-067). Unanimous.
figures: about $8.2 million estimate (councillor, transcript 0:27:37).
reasons: objections-not-planning-grounds: design questions are not what a borrowing hearing decides (Earl Funk)
public: K.P., for the owner of 5 PTH 12 North (a family property), raised design concerns; one household wrote.
seconder: Damian Penner; Bill Hiebert; Susan Penner

title: 2022: 18 planning applications and 3 road closings with no objectors; one retail use denied anyway
summary: With no objection on file and nobody speaking against, council heard By-laws 2191, 2176, 2193 and 2214, subdivisions 8555 and 8706, variances V-2022-01, -03, -09, -10, -11, -13, -17 and -20, and conditional uses CU-2022-01 to -04, plus road closings 2199, 2196 and 2166 (Dec 6, no minutes). Council denied CU-2022-02 (retail in the M1 industrial zone) on its own judgment, denied the unneeded half of V-2022-17, and approved CU-2022-01 and CU-2022-04 only in limited form, each 5-2. The Jan 4 curbside-waste service plan and Apr 5 financial plan hearings drew nobody.
status_detail: 17 of 18 approved (some with conditions); CU-2022-02 denied unanimously (R22-224).
figures: Counted from minutes and output/steinbach_council_motions.csv; Dec 6 road closing from the transcript only.
public: None.
vote: mostly unanimous; R22-077 5-2 (against: Zwaagstra, J. Hiebert); R22-262 5-2 (against: D. Penner, J. Hiebert)
notes: Apr 5, 2022 video has no audio. Reasons for the CU-2022-01/-04 dissents (retail in industrial land) were not reviewed in transcripts.

title: Parking variance for Steinbach Community Outreach affordable housing approved; neighbour's fence and privacy concerns not required
summary: V-2022-02 cut required parking from 40 to 30 stalls for an affordable bachelor/one-bedroom building by Steinbach Community Outreach at 224 Woodhaven Avenue. N.P., whose yard backs onto the site, raised privacy, a fence, theft, people cutting through, and dumpsters. The mayor referred crime and speeding to the RCMP; the City Manager said the zoning by-law requires no fence or buffer between two residential uses. Council approved with conditions tied to the affordable-housing grant, not to her concerns.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R22-052) subject to bachelor/one-bedroom units only, a city affordable-housing grant agreement and a development agreement.
figures: 30 stalls vs 40 required (minutes Mar 1, 2022).
reasons: objections-not-planning-grounds: buffering applies only to incompatible uses; a 40-ft drainage reserve already separates the lots (Troy Warkentin)
public: N.P., a neighbour on Whitby Crescent, objected (privacy, fencing, theft, dumpsters, speeding).

title: Murano Cove side-yard variance tabled two weeks for answers to neighbours' fire and insurance concerns, then approved
summary: A builder put a porch post 2.05 feet from the side lot line (4 feet required), with the eave about half a foot from the line, and applied after the fact (V-2022-23). The neighbour and his brother objected over fire risk, insurance, curb appeal and property value. Councillor Jake Hiebert moved to deny but found no seconder; council tabled the file so staff could report on fire, insurance, measurements and precedent. On Aug 16 staff found no case of a setback variance affecting a neighbour's insurance, and council approved as applied.
status_detail: Tabled Aug 2 (R22-181); approved unanimously Aug 16, 2022 (R22-195) on Jake Hiebert's motion. The objectors' questions changed the timing and the information, not the result.
figures: 2.05 ft vs 4 ft side yard; eave within 0.5 ft (City Manager, transcript Aug 2, 2022 0:26:20).
reasons: staff-recommends: a genuine, honest mistake by a reputable builder (Susan Penner)
public: P.B. (the neighbour) and W.B. (his brother) objected in person on Aug 2; they were not heard again on Aug 16, when council decided on the staff report.
mover: Jake Hiebert (deny, lost); Damian Penner (table); Jake Hiebert (approve)
notes: Jake Hiebert is medium-confidence on the Aug 16 speaker map, so his remarks that day are not quoted.

title: Old Tom Road / Loewen Blvd neighbourhood approved over neighbours' flooding, traffic and density concerns
summary: OCP By-law 2211, rezonings 2212 (commercial mixed use) and 2213 (single-family to high-density) and subdivision 8586 (95 parcels) opened a large development at Old Tom Road and Loewen Boulevard. Neighbours raised creek flooding and drainage, traffic and pedestrian safety, too much high density in phase 1, dust, and uniform fencing; one asked for a traffic study. The R.M. of La Broquerie wrote with drainage concerns and later withdrew its objection. Council approved after the developer's engineers said drainage would improve.
status_detail: Second readings and subdivision approved unanimously Sep 6 (R22-201 to R22-205). By-law 2213 was re-heard Nov 1 after a notice error (no one attended) and passed again (R22-250). Third readings came Jun 6, 2023 (R23-115 to R23-117).
figures: 95 parcels: 30 RSF, 60 RLD, 4 RHD, 1 C-MX (minutes Sep 6, 2022).
reasons: staff-recommends: months of engineering by the city and developer and provincial review (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: roads are improved as development comes (Earl Funk); need-housing: high density is needed for people who cannot afford a house (Susan Penner)
public: R.F., D.E., K.C. and L.C., and J.C. (who said he was not opposed but objected to phase-1 density) spoke; G.P., an adjacent farmland owner, asked for one uniform perimeter fence and said an earlier request 'fell on deaf ears'. The R.M. of La Broquerie objected in writing, then withdrew.
mover: Michael Zwaagstra; Jac Siemens; Susan Penner; Damian Penner
seconder: Susan Penner; Damian Penner; Michael Zwaagstra; Jac Siemens
notes: Third readings are in 2023, outside this period (from the motions CSV).

title: Error in the public notice for By-law 2213 found after the hearing; council rescinds second reading and re-advertises
summary: After the Sep 6, 2022 hearing, staff found an error in the public notice for rezoning By-law 2213 that made a 'material change' to what had been advertised. Councillor Zwaagstra gave notice of motion on Sep 20, council rescinded second reading on Oct 4, notices were reissued and a new hearing was held Nov 1, 2022.
status_detail: Second reading rescinded unanimously (R22-227); new hearing Nov 1 with no one present; second reading given again (R22-250). Earlier letters and objections stayed on file.
reasons: notice-meets-act: notice rules are set by the province and must be followed exactly (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Nobody attended the re-run hearing; the September objectors' comments were kept on file (minutes Nov 1, 2022).
notes: The nature of the error is not stated in the minutes or transcript.

title: 6 First Street / 78 PTH 52 West plan change and rezoning approved 5-2 over Loewen Windows' objection
summary: OCP By-law 2216 (industrial to central business district) and rezoning 2215 (RLD to RMD) allowed a three-storey apartment at 6 First Street and part of 78 PTH 52 West. Loewen Windows objected (too close to a busy highway and intersection, sight lines, appearance); a next-door resident asked about construction noise; three letters were filed. Before the hearing the applicant moved the building from 5 to 8 feet off PTH 52. Councillors Siemens and Jake Hiebert voted against.
status_detail: First reading of 2216 carried 6-1 Oct 4 (R22-229, Siemens against; his motion to deny had no seconder). Second readings 5-2 Nov 1 (R22-251, R22-252). Third readings Jul 4, 2023 (2216 6-1; 2215 unanimous). The 5-to-8-foot setback change was credited by Councillor Zwaagstra as partly addressing concerns.
figures: setback from PTH 52 West 8 ft instead of 5 ft (minutes Nov 1, 2022).
reasons: need-housing: need for multi-family; site would otherwise stay as it is (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: council has already requested lights at Giesbrecht and 52 (Damian Penner); meets-the-plan: RMD is a buffer between industrial/commercial and residential (Susan Penner)
public: Loewen Windows (business) objected in person; C.M., next door, asked about construction noise; L.W., a developer from the R.M. of La Broquerie, asked about buffers and frontage; Swift Communications spoke in favour.
notes: Whether the 8-ft setback was made because of objectors is not stated; the minutes say the applicant made the change.

title: Hotel side-yard variance approved over a neighbouring law office's formal objection
summary: V-2022-26 let the Days Inn at 75 PTH 12 North add extended-stay rooms with an 11'10" side yard where 15 feet is required. The owners of the neighbouring law office and of Penfeld Professional Centre formally objected: an all-glass office would face the addition, parking would spill over, and variances should be exceptional. Council approved, saying a 3.2-foot variance is small and staff found no harm to neighbours.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R22-238); the applicant agreed to drop a room or add a stall to meet parking.
figures: 11'10" vs 15 ft side yard; 73 rooms vs 72 stalls (staff, transcript 0:30:31).
reasons: staff-recommends: staff 'are not in the habit of recommending variances that would have a hugely detrimental impact' (Michael Zwaagstra); notice-meets-act: a properly advertised hearing with notice to nearby owners is part of the rule of law (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: A partner of the neighbouring law firm objected on behalf of two businesses (the law firm and Penfeld Professional Centre); one letter supported the variance.
notes: The objector is identified only by the businesses he spoke for; the law firm is not named because its name includes his surname.

title: 205 McKenzie Ave fourplex given second reading 5-2 over 22 letters and a request to postpone
summary: By-law 2217 rezoned 205 McKenzie Avenue for a four-unit building. C.K. delivered 22 letters of objection (traffic, noise, property values, privacy, drainage), said neighbours had about nine days to organize, and asked for the hearing to be postponed 60-90 days and for a traffic study. Councillor Siemens moved to deny but found no seconder; council gave second reading the same night 5-2, with Siemens and Mayor Funk against.
status_detail: Second reading 5-2 (R22-253). The objections went to the Municipal Board (hearing 2023); third reading Jun 18, 2024 (6-1). The postponement request was not discussed.
figures: 22 letters of objection (minutes Nov 1, 2022); 4 units.
reasons: need-housing: large lots near major streets only redevelop at higher density; impact 'minor' (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: satisfied the garage setback keeps sight lines safe (Jake Hiebert)
public: C.K. spoke for 22 objecting households; V.H. spoke about children's safety. Allegations about notice timing are residents' accounts.
notes: Same night as the inaugural meeting of the 2022-2026 term. Quotes from C.K. are also on the existing report.

title: 2023: 11 planning hearings with no objectors (10 approved, 1 denied on staff advice)
summary: Public reserve closing 2218 (60 Acres Dr); variances V-2023-04, -10, -13, -14, -24; rezonings 2230 (84 McKenzie) and 2234 (385 Loewen Blvd); conditional use CU-2023-01 (animal shelter, 39 Keating Rd); Subdivision 4451-2022-8798 (Heritage Parkway); and V-2023-22 (317 PTH 52 West), which council denied 5-1 although no one objected, after staff recommended denial for drainage reasons. Four Municipal Act hearings on local improvement plans (2220-2223) and the 2023 financial plan hearing drew no one.
status_detail: 10 approved (several with lot-grading or shed-removal conditions set by staff); V-2023-22 denied 5-1 (Bill Hiebert against, R23-251).
figures: Count from minutes 2023 (public hearing blocks); V-2023-22 asked for a 4 ft side yard where 15 ft is required.
reasons: staff-recommends: On V-2023-22: precedent for neighbouring highway lots; neighbours had notice and did not object, but no one knew whether they agreed. (Jac Siemens); precedent: A 15 ft to 4 ft cut is "almost ignoring" the by-law; no drainage plan. (Jake Hiebert)
public: No residents spoke or wrote at these hearings.
notes: Uncontested = no letters or speakers against recorded in the minutes.

title: Three contested 2022 files finished: Municipal Board hearing on 205 McKenzie, third readings for 6 First Street and Old Tom Road
summary: Files heard in 2022 came back in 2023. Objections to the 205 McKenzie Avenue fourplex (By-law 2217, 22 letters in 2022) sent it to the Manitoba Municipal Board, which held its own hearing on April 12, 2023; council sent the City Manager and City Planner to represent the city (R23-063). The Old Tom Road / Loewen Boulevard rezoning (By-law 2213), re-advertised in 2022 after staff found an error in the notice, got third reading on June 6, 2023 (R23-117). The 6 First Street plan amendment and rezoning (By-laws 2216, 2215), objected to by Loewen Windows in 2022, got third reading on July 4, 2023 after ministerial approval.
status_detail: All three went ahead. By-law 2216 carried 5-1 (Jac Siemens against, R23-141); 2215 and 2213 unanimous. By-law 2217 waited for the Municipal Board and got third reading only on June 18, 2024 (see 2024 item).
figures: Municipal Board hearing Apr 12-14, 2023 (R23-063); 2216 third reading 5-1 (R23-141).
reasons: meets-the-plan: Third readings followed ministerial approval of the plan amendment and execution of development agreements. (council)
public: The 2022 objectors were Loewen Windows (business, on 6 First Street: highway proximity, traffic, visibility) and 22 households on McKenzie Avenue.
mover: R23-063 Bill Hiebert; R23-141 Damian Penner
seconder: R23-063 Jac Siemens; R23-141 Jake Hiebert
notes: The Municipal Board's 2023 decision on By-law 2217 was not found in the meetings searched. Susan Penner absent Jul 4, 2023.

title: 2023: two hearings where neighbours asked questions but did not object (Lund Road four-storey variance, McKenzie Avenue subdivision)
summary: At V-2023-07 (188 Lund Road, four storeys instead of three) the owner of the neighbouring lot asked about parking; the applicant said an approved parking and site plan existed. At Subdivision 4451-2023-8850 (84 McKenzie Avenue, 70 lots) a Coral Crescent resident asked what would be built behind her yard and staff explained setbacks. Both were approved unanimously.
status_detail: Approved as applied (R23-124, R23-159).
reasons: staff-recommends: Questions answered at the hearing; no objection recorded. (Troy Warkentin)
public: J.I. (owner of 180 Lund Road) asked about parking; N.T. asked about the homes planned behind her yard.

title: Third Street 32-unit rezoning denied after a 40-plus-name petition and 13 objectors
themes: rezoning; infill; petition; letters; tabled; consultation; staff-recommendation
summary: Kingdom Home Building Inc. applied (By-law 2231) to rezone 360, 364 and 368 Third Street from low to medium density for a three-storey, 32-unit rental building. Four letters came in (two after the agenda was printed), 13 neighbours objected in person and T.B. handed in a petition with "over 40 signatures". The applicant, who had not consulted most neighbours, asked mid-hearing to table the file for two months so he could go door to door, then offered to withdraw. Council refused to adjourn, let every resident who wanted to speak finish, and denied second reading unanimously.
status_detail: Second reading denied unanimously (R23-160); the by-law died. Objections changed the outcome (the applicant also asked for denial once he heard the opposition). The mayor asked that the petition be kept on file. A similar application for the same lots had been refused about 10 years earlier.
figures: 4 written items of correspondence plus a petition of "over 40 signatures" and 13 objectors in person (minutes items 12.2, 14-29); 32 units, three storeys (minutes item 14, 16); first reading Jul 4, 2023 (R23-139).
public: Objectors (L.A., P.P., T.B., G.F., K.P., S.P., N.V.G., M.R., S.A., T.L., G.R., A.G., K.V.G.) said a three-storey, 32-unit building did not fit a single-family block and the city's own infill policy, and raised traffic, lost green space, lighting, property values and problems at the owner's existing rentals (allegations about the rentals are unproven). T.B. insisted residents still be heard after the applicant asked to withdraw. The applicant L.W. said he preferred answering residents at the hearing rather than going door to door.
notes: Thirteen residents spoke against; counts from minutes items 14-29. Jake Hiebert absent (minutes attendance).

title: Minor variances approved by staff without a hearing, reported to council twice a year
summary: Small variances are decided by the Planning and Zoning Department, not at a public hearing; council accepts the list twice a year (Jan-Jun 2023 with minor subdivisions; Jul-Dec 2023; Dec 2023-Jun 2024; Jul-Dec 2024). At the 40 First Street hearing staff said a lot-width shortfall "could be approved by administration".
status_detail: Lists accepted unanimously as information (R23-172, R23-267, R24-150, R24-253).
figures: Lists attached to minutes; numbers not counted.
notes: How neighbours are notified of minor variances was not discussed in the meetings searched and is unverified.

title: First Street lane closing passed 5-2 over a written objection from a neighbouring owner
summary: By-law 2232 closed an undeveloped public lane behind First Street lots (used for decades as a public drain) so it could become a plan of works, a condition of a subdivision council had approved in July 2023 for a multi-family project at 6 First Street / 78 PTH 52 West. One letter of objection came from a neighbouring owner who wanted the lane for future access; it arrived after the agenda was printed. Staff said it had to be treated as an objection but did not stop third reading. Nobody spoke at the hearing.
status_detail: Second and third readings carried 5-2 (R23-226, R23-227); Jac Siemens and Jake Hiebert against. Approved as proposed; the objection did not change the outcome.
figures: One written objection (minutes 9.2); first reading Oct 3, 2023 (R23-198).
reasons: staff-recommends: The lane has always been a drain; closing it fulfils a subdivision condition council already set; an objection does not bar third reading. (Troy Warkentin); objections-not-planning-grounds: Every affected lot already has street access; the closing is consistent with what council approved. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: One written objection from a neighbouring property owner and developer (initials not given in the record), who said his lots would lose possible rear access; staff said all lots front on First Street or Giesbrecht Street.
notes: Notice for a lane closing is given under the Municipal Act (City Manager), not the Planning Act. The objector is not named in the minutes; the transcript gives a surname only, so no initials are given.

title: 600 Main Street sixplex approved; objector's requested fence condition not imposed
summary: By-law 2238 rezoned 600 Main Street from low to medium density for a sixplex, with a 70 ft lot-width variance (V-2023-23). One neighbour, P.K., said a sixplex was "a little aggressive" (a fourplex would be fine) and asked that a fence blocking back-lane access be a condition of approval; one resident spoke in favour. The owner agreed to a fence. Councillor Susan Penner, moving approval, said she did not want a fence required; the mayor left the buffer to the owner and neighbourhood.
status_detail: Second and third readings and the variance carried unanimously (R24-004, R24-005, R24-006), subject only to a development agreement. The objector's condition was not written into the resolutions; the applicant's promise of a buffer was informal.
figures: One objector, one supporter (minutes 8.1-8.2); lot 70 ft vs 75 ft required.
reasons: meets-the-plan: On Main Street, a buffer to the homes behind; other multi-family nearby. (Susan Penner); need-housing: Older areas are evolving to more multi-family through infill. (Earl Funk)
public: P.K. objected to the unit count and back-lane traffic and asked for a fence condition; H.W. spoke in favour.
mover: Susan Penner; Jac Siemens; Damian Penner
seconder: Bill Hiebert; Michael Zwaagstra; Michael Zwaagstra
notes: Jake Hiebert absent. The development agreement was not reviewed, so whether it includes a buffer is unverified.

title: Wyndham Estate Drive public reserve closing approved over a formal objection
summary: By-law 2237 closed part of a public reserve so Stonebridge Development Corporation could create one more lot. Two letters came in; D.M. formally objected, asking how the city benefits and whether the extra lot overloads the single road access; P.K. asked about servicing. Staff said green space remains above the requirement and the net lot count does not rise. Approved unanimously.
status_detail: Second and third readings carried unanimously (R24-007, R24-008), subject to the related subdivision. Objection did not change the outcome.
figures: 2 written items (minutes 15.2); one formal objector in person.
reasons: need-housing: One more lot means more housing; green space still exceeds the by-law. (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: The lot does not add to the approved lot count on a net basis. (Troy Warkentin)
public: D.M. formally objected (benefit to the city, traffic on the single access road); P.K. asked about servicing a new road.
vote: unanimous (mayor out of the room for second reading; Jake Hiebert absent)

title: Truck yard at 45 Tower Avenue denied after about 17 letters and 8 objecting speakers
summary: S.S. applied for a conditional use (CU-2023-02) to run a 19-truck freight yard on M1 industrial land next to the Deerfield / Wyndham homes, a school walking path and a middle school, plus a variance (V-2023-25) for barbed wire already installed. Staff noted the residential buffer. About 17 letters arrived, many on the day of the meeting; eight neighbours spoke on noise, lights, dust, wells, child safety and property values. One said he learned of the hearing by email that day. Council denied both unanimously.
status_detail: Conditional use denied (R24-009) and barbed-wire variance denied (R24-010), both unanimous. Objections changed the outcome: councillors cited the neighbours' concerns and the closeness of homes.
figures: "approximately 17 written items of correspondence" (minutes 22.2); 8 objectors in person (minutes 23.2-27); 19 trucks, 4 of 22 acres (minutes 22.3, 28).
public: D.P., G.P., J.L., S.U., D.M., C.W., K.D. and H.W. objected or raised concerns (noise, 24-hour operation, lights, dust, well water, child safety on the school path, property values). D.M. said he had heard of the hearing only by email that day. Residents asked whether council had read letters that came in that day; the mayor said council read them from 6 p.m.
vote: unanimous (Jake Hiebert absent; mayor out for the variance vote)
notes: Jake Hiebert absent. Staff recommended approving the variance "subject to any new evidence"; the conditional-use recommendation is truncated in the transcript and not confirmed.

title: Home Street 32-unit rezoning approved 4-3 over a 43-name petition; sent to the Municipal Board
themes: rezoning; infill; petition; letters; municipal-board; consultation; notice
summary: Kingdom Home Building Inc. applied (By-law 2241) to rezone 268 and 274 Home Street, across from the hospital and near the event centre, for a three-storey, 32-unit building. Eight items of correspondence came in, including a petition with 43 names. The developer said he left invitations at 14-15 nearby homes for a round-table less than a week before and no one came; adjacent neighbours said they never got one. Twelve residents spoke against and four for. Second reading carried 4-3. Objections then sent the by-law to the Manitoba Municipal Board, which held a hearing in August 2024.
status_detail: Second reading carried 4-3 (R24-061; against: Damian Penner, Jake Hiebert, Michael Zwaagstra). Referred to the Municipal Board; council delegated staff to its Aug 14-16, 2024 hearing (R24-159). Third reading not found in the meetings searched (through 2024). Objections did not change council's vote but triggered the Board review.
figures: 8 items of correspondence incl. a 43-name petition (minutes 6.3); 12 objectors, 4 supporters in person (minutes 6.7-6.23); 27 underground + 28 surface stalls (minutes 6.4).
reasons: need-housing: Healthy downtown, near hospital and event centre, elevator for seniors; benefits outweigh costs. (Susan Penner); meets-the-plan: "its own transition zone" between hospital and homes; large old lots cannot be rebuilt as single-family. (Jac Siemens); traffic-manageable: Apartments near his own street generate little traffic (medium-confidence speaker). (Bill Hiebert)
public: Objectors (K.D., D.T., G.W., D.W., S.R., A.K., M.P., J.B., L.P., E.D., A.T., E.W.) cited fit with a well-kept single-family area outside the transitional zone, affordable starter homes, traffic, privacy, mature trees and construction fatigue from the event centre and hospital. K.D. and E.D. (adjacent) said they got no invitation from the developer. Supporters G.S., J.W., H.W. and C.S. cited walkability, downtown vitality and rental options.
vote: 4-3 (against: Damian Penner, Jake Hiebert, Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: Bill Hiebert is a medium-confidence speaker in the map; his reasons are paraphrased, not quoted. Third reading and the Municipal Board result were not found in the 2023-2024 meetings; the project returned for a height variance in 2025 (existing report).

title: 2024: 15 planning hearings with no objectors, all approved
summary: Public reserve closings 2235 and 2246; rezonings 2236 and 2250; subdivisions 4451-2021-8575 and 4451-2024-8941; variances V-2024-01, -05, -07, -09, -12, -13; conditional uses CU-2024-03 (caretaker suite, one supporter), CU-2024-05 (electronic sign) and CU-2024-06 (daycare). V-2024-05 legalised a sunroom built without a permit, with a $1,000 fine; eight items of correspondence were on file and members said no neighbour objected. The 2024 financial plan hearing drew no one.
status_detail: All approved, several with conditions (development agreement, lot grading, residential use kept accessory, fine).
figures: Count from 2024 minutes; V-2024-05 fine $1,000 (R24-118).
reasons: staff-recommends: For after-the-fact variances, asks whether council would approve it new and whether neighbours object. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: No objections recorded.
notes: Uncontested = no objection recorded in minutes or transcript. The content of the eight V-2024-05 letters was not read into the record.

title: 330 First Street 15-unit apartment approved over two neighbours' objections
summary: W.N., for the owner, applied for a conditional use (CU-2024-01) to build a 15-unit residential building in the C2 commercial zone and a variance (V-2024-02) to drop the required main-floor commercial. One letter came in; R.B. raised privacy, traffic and rental problems and E.B. formally objected over privacy, noise and lighting; S.J. spoke in support. The applicant described privacy fencing, bedroom-only side windows and a 126 ft separation. Both approved unanimously.
status_detail: CU approved (R24-062) and variance approved (R24-063), unanimous, subject to a development agreement. Objections did not change the outcome.
figures: 1 written item (minutes 9.2); 2 objectors, 1 supporter in person (minutes 9.4-9.6); 15 units.
reasons: meets-the-plan: Zoned C2 and in the CBD transitional zone; a commercial building of the same size could go there anyway. (Michael Zwaagstra); staff-recommends: Similar applications approved before; recommended approval. (Troy Warkentin)
public: R.B. (concerns: privacy, traffic, rentals) and E.B. (formal objection: privacy, noise, lighting, garbage); S.J. spoke in favour.

title: Province flags that an amended subdivision needs a public hearing; council holds one
summary: Council had approved Subdivision 4451-2021-8575 (195 Park Road West) without a hearing. When a road widening was added, the province's Community Planning office said a public hearing was required, so one was held. No one came.
status_detail: Approved unanimously after the hearing (R24-074).
reasons: notice-meets-act: Hearing held because the provincial planners said the Act required it. (Troy Warkentin)
public: No one attended.

title: 205 McKenzie fourplex gets third reading 6-1 after the Municipal Board process
summary: By-law 2217 (fourplex at 205 McKenzie Avenue across from SRSS), approved 5-2 at second reading in 2022 over 22 letters and referred to the Municipal Board in 2023, returned once the development agreement was signed. Jac Siemens spoke against for the third time (school-zone congestion, parking, garbage pickup).
status_detail: Third reading carried 6-1 (R24-129; Jac Siemens against). Approved as applied.
figures: Seven on-site stalls (Siemens, transcript 1:41:20).
reasons: meets-the-plan: Density beside a school is where density belongs. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: No new public input at third reading.
notes: The Municipal Board's decision itself was not reviewed.

title: 2024: Main Street six-storey building approved after one letter and a parking question
summary: CU-2024-04 and V-2024-04 (362/366 Main Street, Avedo Inc.) allowed a six-storey, 78 ft mixed-use building with 32 suites where five storeys and 50 ft are allowed. One letter came in (content not stated) and E.K. asked about parking; staff said the plan met the parking rules. Every member praised it as the downtown density council had planned for. Approved unanimously.
status_detail: Approved as applied (R24-116, R24-117).
figures: 1 item of correspondence (minutes 8.1); 32 suites, 67 stalls (transcript 0:31:34-0:31:43).
reasons: meets-the-plan: Central business district vision of commercial below, residential above. (council)
public: E.K. asked how many suites and whether parking was enough.
notes: Whether the letter objected is not recorded.

title: 40 First Street rezoning: neighbours' traffic and drainage questions, second reading carried
summary: Kingdom Home Building Inc. applied (By-law 2253) to rezone 40 First Street for a multi-family building. E.B., owner of the next property, asked whether the drawing is what will be built and about green space; G.W. raised traffic and existing drainage problems on Giesbrecht Street. Staff said the 72 ft lot (75 ft required) would need only a minor variance that administration can approve without a hearing. Second reading carried unanimously.
status_detail: Second reading unanimous (R24-207); third reading Feb 17, 2026 (R26-044). Concerns did not change the outcome.
figures: Two residents with concerns (minutes 6.4, 6.6); lot 72 ft vs 75 ft (minutes 6.5).
reasons: staff-recommends: Lot-width shortfall handled by an administrative minor variance. (administration)
public: E.B. (adjacent owner: design certainty, demolition timing, green space) and G.W. (traffic, drainage).
notes: No transcript for Nov 5, 2024 (video not transcribed); minutes only.

title: Plan and zoning by-law rewrite: engagement promised, shelters made a conditional use so neighbours get a hearing
summary: The Official Community Plan and zoning by-law review began in spring 2023. On Dec 3, 2024 council endorsed the draft changes (R24-234): public engagement in mid-January 2025, first reading in February and hearings in March. Members highlighted making an "emergency residential shelter" a conditional use, so neighbours get a public hearing they did not have when such a shelter counted as a permitted social service. The same draft makes offices, restaurants and clinics permitted (no hearing) in the transitional district and cuts downtown parking by a third.
status_detail: Direction to proceed carried (R24-234). The engagement happened in 2025 (open house January 2025; hearing April 1, 2025, per the existing report). Turnout and survey results were not reported to council in 2023-2024.
figures: Zoning by-law cut from 155 to 106 pages (Damian Penner, transcript 0:18:33).
reasons: already-consulted: Open house and a formal hearing still to come. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Not a hearing; no public speakers. The Sept 27, 2023 visioning workshop and survey (SteinbachOnline) were not discussed at council in the meetings searched.
notes: Mayor Funk absent; Zwaagstra chaired.

title: City files a formal objection to an RM of Hanover rezoning on its border
summary: Council used the objection process itself: it authorised a formal objection to RM of Hanover By-law 2578-24, which would rezone land along PTH 12 North already subdivided and built on, against Hanover's plan, provincial policy and the annexation agreement's requirement to consult Steinbach. The city had also objected to the subdivision in 2024, which Hanover approved anyway.
status_detail: Objection authorised unanimously (R24-246) ahead of Hanover's Jan 8, 2025 hearing; the outcome is outside this period.
notes: Hearing date given in the transcript as "January 8th, 2018 ... 2025" (corrected by the City Manager).

title: Mailed notices add a plain-language Q&A, online and QR-code submissions
summary: From late 2024 the city's mailed hearing notice to owners within 100 m includes a plain-language Q&A explaining hearings and that written comments count; by January 2025 it accepted submissions through the city website or a QR code. Notices also appear on the city's public notices page with an email subscription. Petitions 'are accepted but will not be considered a formal objection'; documents are viewable at City Hall 9-4 weekdays.
status_detail: In use through 2026; minutes record 'notices pursuant to The Planning Act had been completed' at every hearing. The 330 McKenzie hearing (Oct 2026) drew 62 written submissions, the most in the period.
figures: Council packages Nov 19, 2024 and Jan 21, 2025 (per existing report).
reasons: notice-meets-act: notices meet the Planning Act minimum (staff (minutes))
notes: Not re-verified against the packages in this pass; taken from the existing report.

title: 2025: about 20 hearings with no objectors on record, almost all approved
themes: variance; conditional-use; subdivision; rezoning; staff-recommendation; notice
summary: Most 2025 planning hearings drew no one but the applicant: council heard the file, the mayor asked three times for 'comments, questions, or objections', and decided the same night. Counted from the minutes: 18 site-specific applications with no objector and no correspondence against (subdivision 4451-2024-9041 August Cove; By-law 2260, 79 & 85 First St; V-2025-03, 430 Rockwood; V-2025-04, 333 Loewen Blvd; V-2025-05, 7 Brandt; V-2025-06, 85 Acres Dr; V-2025-08, 896 Main; V-2025-10 and V-2025-11, Essex Dr signs; CU-2025-02, 16 Pioneer Rd; V-2025-13, 13 PTH 52 W; V-2025-14 and V-2025-20, 22 Country View Lane; CU-2025-04, Elmdale St signs; V-2025-22, 116/118 Sterling Cres; V-2025-30, 53 Grandview Dr; subdivision 4451-2025-9173 Park Hill; CU-2025-01, 86 Industrial Rd; V-2025-24, 11-40 North Gate Dr). Two more had one item of correspondence whose content the minutes do not give (By-law 2268 Rosebrook Trail; V-2025-36, 49 Market Blvd), and at one (CU-2025-03) a resident only asked questions.
status_detail: All approved except CU-2025-01 (retail thrift store in the industrial park) and V-2025-24 (Suncor landscaping reduction), which council denied with no objectors present, and CU-2025-03 (see 2025-2026-denials-without-objectors). V-2025-22 passed 4-3 with no objectors (split on the city engineer's stormwater and precedent concerns). By-laws 2262 and 2268 got second and third reading the same night as the hearing.
figures: Counts from 2025 minutes (packets and PDFs for Jun 3 and Jul 15, 2025); Municipal Act hearings (LIP 2255, SSP 2257, financial plan) not counted.
public: No objectors. Applicants or their builders presented; V-2025-14's owner filed 4 letters of support.
notes: Counting is from the minutes' 'There was no one present at the public hearing with questions or concerns' and correspondence lines; transcripts were not read for every uncontested hearing.

title: Council denied four requests that no neighbour objected to
summary: Objections are not the only route to a denial. With no objector present, council denied retail in the industrial park twice (CU-2025-01, Adult and Teen Challenge thrift store at 86 Industrial Rd, Feb 18, 2025; CU-2025-03, The Home Workshop showroom at 123 Industrial Rd, Jul 15, 2025), a 50% cut in street-edge landscaping for a Suncor station (V-2025-24, Sep 16, 2025), and the caretaker's residence part of CU-2026-10 at 75 Industrial Rd (Sep 1, 2026). At CU-2025-03 a resident, G.S., asked only whether city industrial lots are subsidized; the mayor said they are sold at cost to support manufacturing.
status_detail: All four denied: R25-034 and R25-178 unanimous; R25-144 5-1 (Siemens against; his motion to approve with conditions died for want of a seconder); R26-181 unanimous (industrial multi-use approved, residence denied).
figures: Minutes Feb 18, Jul 15, Sep 16, 2025; Sep 1, 2026.
reasons: meets-the-plan: industrial lots exist to support manufacturing; retail is only a conditional use there (council (minutes, mayor at CU-2025-03))
public: No objectors; G.S. asked questions at CU-2025-03 (minutes).
seconder: J. Hiebert; D. Penner; D. Penner; J. Hiebert
notes: CU-2025-03 (Jul 15, 2025) has no transcript; minutes only.

title: Home St apartment allowed a fourth (parking) storey over neighbours' objections, 3-2
summary: A year after the contested 268/274 Home St rezoning (approved 4-3 in 2024, then reviewed by the Municipal Board), the builder asked for a fourth storey of partly underground parking (V-2025-02). One letter of objection was on file; four neighbours from three households spoke against it (privacy, sunlight, trees, traffic, construction fatigue) and one read a letter from a fourth household. Council approved it subject to the parking level being no more than 1 metre above grade.
status_detail: Approved 3-2 (R25-049). The 1-metre condition, added by Councillor D. Penner's amendment, matched what the applicant said the building code allowed; it clarified the design rather than responding to the objectors' concerns.
figures: Building roughly 47 ft at the peak (applicant, transcript 1:20:54); 1 objection letter on file (minutes 12.2).
reasons: meets-the-plan: downtown infill density is what the plan calls for; underground parking means fewer surface stalls (Susan Penner); precedent: voted on the principle that an underground parking level should not count as a storey; rezoning already decided (Damian Penner); need-housing: neighbourhoods adjust once buildings are up; area is in long-term transition (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: B.B., W.K., D.K. and E.W. (three households) objected in person; B.B. read a letter from a fourth household; one written objection (minutes). D.K. said he expected nothing they said would sway the vote.
vote: 3-2 (against: Michael Zwaagstra, Jake Hiebert); Siemens and B. Hiebert not recorded as voting
notes: Who was absent is not stated in the extract read; only five votes are recorded.

title: Sixplex rezoning at 189 Hanover St denied after 8 letters and 5 speakers against
summary: By-law 2261 would have rezoned a mid-block lot from RLD to RMD for a two-storey sixplex. The applicants had visited 25 neighbouring properties and needed no variances. Eight letters of objection were filed; four neighbours spoke against (character, traffic, parking, privacy, sunlight, property values), one asked whether the city aimed to replace single-family homes, and two spoke in favour. Council denied the rezoning unanimously, saying the block was not ready to transition.
status_detail: Denied unanimously (R25-056). One of two applications in the period denied after strong objection.
figures: 8 items of correspondence objecting (minutes 6.2); 10 stalls plus 3 garages (minutes 6.4).
public: G.B., C.S., J.R. and S.K. objected in person; H.D. asked about a broader goal of replacing single-family homes; J.W. and S.T. supported the project (minutes).

title: Province raises the bar for formal objections to 300 and ends Municipal Board hearings
summary: Before June 2025, 25 objections to a zoning by-law or plan sent it to the Municipal Board for a hearing (explained by the city's consultant on Apr 1, 2025; Steinbach's new zoning by-law went this way). S.M. 2025, c. 3 (assented June 3, 2025) raised the threshold to at least 300 eligible persons in a municipality of Steinbach's size, and a 2026 amendment (Bulletin 2026-17, in force June 1, 2026) has the Board review the record without a hearing and send council non-binding recommendations. Variances and conditional uses remain final at council. No Steinbach by-law reached the Board after the change, including the 330 McKenzie rezoning that drew 62 letters (council denied it anyway).
status_detail: Provincial change, not a council decision. Council did not discuss it in the meetings searched, and the city's notice was not found to explain the new threshold.
figures: 25 → 300 eligible objectors (S.M. 2025, c. 3); Board 'must not hold a hearing' from June 1, 2026 (Bulletin 2026-17), per the existing report's legal research.
notes: Legislative details taken from the existing verified report (answers/public-notice); not re-fetched. No transcript in 2025-2026 mentions the 300 threshold.

title: New Official Community Plan and zoning by-law: engagement described, a resident asks who knew
summary: At the Apr 1, 2025 hearings on the Official Community Plan (By-law 2244) and Zoning By-law 2245, the city's consultant described the 2023-2025 engagement (visioning workshop, stakeholder interviews, surveys, open house) and the Planning Act objection steps. A resident, A.A., asked where the plan notice was posted and how many ordinary residents knew about it; the mayor said there was no survey of that and the city could do a better job of communicating. Three objections to the OCP were filed. The OCP got first and second reading that night and third reading on Sep 16, 2025.
status_detail: OCP adopted (R25-069, R25-070; third reading R25-184, Sep 16, 2025). No turnout or survey results were reported to council in the meetings searched.
figures: OCP: 3 items of correspondence objecting (minutes 6.2). Planning Act then: 25 objections triggered a second-objection step (consultant, 0:21:06).
reasons: notice-meets-act: all legislative advertising requirements were met and documents were online (K.S. (WSP)); already-consulted: workshop, interviews, surveys and open house held as the Act requires (K.S. (WSP))
public: A.A. asked about notice and awareness (medium-confidence speaker label; minutes record his question). R.J. objected on broader political grounds; A.B. objected to a downtown parking/cycling idea she had not heard about.
notes: K.S. is the city's consultant (WSP), not city staff; role set to staff for lack of a consultant category.

title: New zoning by-law: shelters made a conditional use, objections send it to the Municipal Board
summary: Zoning By-law 2245 (replacing By-law 2100) made 'emergency residential shelter' a conditional use, which means a public hearing for any future shelter; the consultant had recommended keeping it a permitted use. Supporters and objectors spoke on Apr 1, 2025, many about The INN's proposed transitional housing at 447 Main St. The mayor said hearing from everyone was the fairest approach. Enough objections were filed to send the by-law to the Manitoba Municipal Board (hearing Oct 1-3, 2025; council delegated the City Manager and City Planner). The Board ordered no changes and council gave third reading on Jan 20, 2026. A follow-up amendment, By-law 2275, defined transitional housing and made it a conditional use in seven zones (Jun 2, 2026; no correspondence).
status_detail: Adopted as amended (R25-071, R25-072; Board delegation R25-181; third reading R26-015, unanimous). By-law 2275 passed second and third reading Jun 2, 2026 (R26-111, R26-112).
figures: 'Several items' of correspondence for and against (minutes 10.2); Board hearing Oct 1-3, 2025 (R25-181).
reasons: already-consulted: the Board looked at the objections and found the by-law 'good as it is' (Michael Zwaagstra); process: conditional use lets everyone be heard on a specific project (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: L.D. (The INN board) said The INN was not included in early discussions; T.C., L.C., C.G. and T.B. objected; B.U., K.U. and B.B. spoke in favour. T.C. asked whether the 25 objections could be written or in person; the mayor said both, received by the end of the hearing.
seconder: D. Penner; J. Hiebert; B. Hiebert; J. Hiebert
notes: The number of objections filed and the Board's order were not read; the by-law's referral predates the June 3, 2025 change to 300 objections. Third reading was pulled from the Jan 6, 2026 agenda (R26-001) and given Jan 20.

title: 286 Henry St rezoning approved; corner setback part of the variance denied
summary: By-law 2262 rezoned 286 Henry St to RMD with a lot-width variance (V-2025-07). One neighbour, C.M., raised the current owners' poor upkeep; the applicant brought two letters of support and said the six lots across were tenant-occupied. Council approved the site width but denied the 4-ft corner side-yard setback, and gave the rezoning second and third reading the same night.
status_detail: Variance partly approved (R25-093); rezoning passed second and third reading (R25-094, R25-095). The corner setback denial did not respond to the neighbour's maintenance concern; the applicant had said the site plan worked without it.
figures: Site width 64.5 ft vs 75 required; corner setback 4 ft vs 8 (minutes).
public: C.M. (287 Henry St) questioned upkeep (minutes).
vote: unanimous (R25-093 vote not recorded in minutes)
notes: Transcript not read for this item; minutes only. C.M. returned in Oct 2026 on the next lot (2026-288-henry-street).

title: Missing item in a variance notice found; decision held for a second hearing
summary: On Aug 5, 2025 the City Manager told council that the residual lot at 22 Country View Lane also needed a site-width variance, which had been left out of the advertising. Council completed the hearing but postponed the decision until a second, properly noticed hearing (V-2025-20) on Sep 2, then approved both.
status_detail: Both variances approved Sep 2, 2025 (R25-170, R25-171). Staff caught and corrected their own notice error.
figures: Site width 62 ft vs 100 required (minutes).
public: No objectors; owner filed 4 letters of support.

title: Flooded residents told to book a delegation rather than speak
summary: Residents flooded on Sep 11, 2025 came to the Sep 16 meeting hoping to speak. The mayor said they could not speak that night, asked them to book a delegation and to pick one person to speak; two residents presented as delegations on Oct 21, 2025.
status_detail: Delegations heard Oct 21, 2025 (minutes). No public question period was offered.
reasons: process: residents speak through booked delegations (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: Flooded residents (unnamed in the record read).
notes: Oct 21, 2025 delegations from the minutes (existing report); not re-read here.

title: Studio apartments at 635/641 Main St approved with fewer parking stalls, 5-2
summary: By-law 2266 rezoned two Main St lots to RMD and V-2025-32 allowed 45 stalls where 59 were required, for small studio units. One neighbouring household raised lighting and dogs and later said it was glad the building would be two storeys with a flat roof; the builder confirmed downward lighting. The split on council was over parking policy, not objections.
status_detail: Rezoning second reading unanimous (R25-221), parking variance 5-2 (R25-222), third reading Jan 20, 2026 (R26-012).
figures: 45 stalls vs 59 required; units under 400 sq ft; target rent about $800 (minutes 13.2).
reasons: need-housing: parking rules must adapt to affordable studio units (Susan Penner)
public: C.S. and N.S. (630 Wilson St) raised lighting, dogs and building size (minutes).

title: Residents ask to see traffic, drainage and sewer studies; developer studies stay unpublished
summary: At several hearings residents asked whether traffic or drainage studies existed and for independent review. Staff said no traffic impact study is generally required for infill (Dec 2025), that city traffic counts and the climate risk assessment would be public (Mar 2026), and that development drainage studies are done by consultants under contract to the developer (Jul 2026). M.R.'s request for a third-party study of Lift Station 1 was not taken up.
status_detail: No independent review or publication of developer studies was offered in the meetings searched.
reasons: objections-not-planning-grounds: engineering reviewed by the city engineer against standard models (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: R.P. (Dec 2025), M.R. and G.R. (Jul 2026) asked for studies.
notes: Related quotes are in 2025-first-street-conditional-use and 2026-stone-bridge-seniors.

title: 190-206 First St: apartments and a five-storey variance approved despite neighbours' traffic and sewer questions
summary: CU-2025-05 allowed multifamily in a C1 zone and V-2025-35 removed the main-floor commercial requirement and allowed five storeys. The developer filed three letters of support from nearby owners. Two neighbours, R.P. and J.G., raised traffic on William Ave and First St, sewer capacity, parking, stormwater and sight lines; R.P. asked whether a traffic impact study was done. The City Manager said none was required and the existing system could service the development.
status_detail: Both approved unanimously (R25-248, R25-249), subject to a development agreement.
figures: Two buildings, 3 and 5 storeys (minutes 12.2); First St designed for 1,000-4,000 vehicles/day (minutes 12.6).
reasons: traffic-manageable: First St is a collector; no traffic study required for this type of application (Troy Warkentin, City Manager); need-housing: reasonable plan, developer consulted neighbours (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: R.P. (185 First St) and J.G. (226 First St) raised questions and concerns; three owners wrote in support (minutes).

title: 2026: 15 hearings with no objectors, all approved (one in part)
summary: Hearings with no objector and no correspondence against: CU-2025-06/V-2025-38, 31 Loewen Blvd (Jan 6); CU-2026-01 Trailblazers, 119/123 Industrial Rd; CU-2026-02 ROC Eastman; V-2026-07, 225 Kroeker; CU-2026-04, 840 Main; CU-2026-05 and CU-2026-06 (May 19); public reserve and road closings 2278 and 2279; CU-2026-07 Maplewood Manor; CU-2026-08 SCU sign; CU-2026-09 fleet services; V-2026-17, 210 Hanover Rd W; CU-2026-10, 75 Industrial Rd; V-2026-21, 31 Loewen Blvd (Oct 20). V-2026-08 (135 Harmony Lane) had one item of correspondence of unstated content. Text amendment By-law 2275 also had none.
status_detail: All approved; CU-2026-10's caretaker's residence was denied. V-2026-07 passed 4-1 (J. Hiebert against) with no objectors.
figures: Counts from 2026 minutes (PDF for May 19) and the Oct 20 transcript.
reasons: staff-recommends: no objections and no staff concerns make a variance appropriate (Oct 20) (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: None.
notes: Oct 20, 2026 minutes not yet available; vote on V-2026-21 from transcript only (carried).

title: 185 Friesen Ave seniors' building: hearing adjourned twice, then approved with more parking
themes: conditional-use; variance; infill; tabled; conditions; letters
summary: Steinbach Housing Inc. asked for multifamily in a C1 zone (CU-2026-03) and a variance (V-2026-05) for seven storeys, 10 parking stalls instead of 150, and a 20-ft front yard, on green space held under a 1989 development-agreement caveat. Three letters came in; R.L. objected for 193 Friesen Ave (height, privacy, green space, the caveat). On staff's recommendation council adjourned on Mar 17 for parking information (6-1, Siemens against, who wanted to decide and honour the 1989 agreement), then again on Apr 21 at the applicant's request. On Jun 2 the plan came back at 84 units with parking at one stall per unit; R.L., speaking for six households, asked for neighbours in design meetings, early street rebuilding, green space and no pile driving. Council approved both.
status_detail: Approved Jun 2 (R26-109 unanimous; R26-110 5-2) with parking raised from 10 stalls to 1 per unit. The parking change came from staff's and council's concerns, which residents shared; the residents' requested conditions (design meetings, no pile driving, green space) were not put in the motion. Zwaagstra's amendment to deny the parking variance died for want of a seconder.
figures: 91 → 84 units; 10 stalls of 150 required → ratio 1:1 (minutes Mar 17 and Jun 2); 3 items of correspondence (minutes 15.2); waitlist of almost 200 (transcript Jun 2, 0:39:03).
reasons: need-housing: seniors' housing waitlist outweighs green space (Jun 2) (Jac Siemens); need-housing: benefit to the community outweighs the cost (Susan Penner); meets-the-plan: area designated transitional in the central business district (Jac Siemens)
public: R.L. and R.L. (193 Friesen) objected on Mar 17; on Jun 2 R.L. spoke for six households and P. (174 Friesen) raised parking and truck traffic (minutes).
seconder: J. Hiebert; B. Hiebert; S. Penner; Siemens
vote: R26-059 6-1 (against: Jac Siemens); R26-110 5-2 (against: Michael Zwaagstra, Bill Hiebert)
notes: Whether the 1989 caveat was discharged was not found in the meetings searched.

title: 48 units at 492-506 McKenzie Ave approved over a petition and seven objectors
summary: By-law 2273 rezoned three large lots on McKenzie Ave from RLD to RMD for three 16-unit buildings. Six items of correspondence came in, including support letters from some neighbours and the church behind; H.K. presented a 'quite lengthy petition' and seven households objected in person (character, no transition from bungalows, sewer backups in 2024 and 2025, truck traffic, U-turns, snow, privacy). P.K. asked for a two-storey limit. Council approved with no conditions beyond the development agreement, noting no variances were requested.
status_detail: Second reading unanimous Apr 7 (R26-068); third reading Sep 1, 2026 (R26-184). No Municipal Board referral (300-objector threshold).
figures: 48 units, 80 parking spaces (minutes 6.4, 8); 6 items of correspondence (minutes 6.2).
reasons: meets-the-plan: no variances requested; all regulations followed (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: collector street 75 m from a major intersection (Damian Penner); need-housing: benefit to the city outweighs neighbours' concerns (Damian Penner); precedent: many precedents for infill next to single-family homes (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: H.K. (petition), A.R., C.V.B., R.W., J.D., P.K. and H.H. objected; B.D. (Sommerfeld Church) raised concerns without objecting; G.S. supported (minutes).

title: Lund Rd: a two-storey cap from a 2013 hearing lifted to three storeys
summary: V-2026-13 let 80 and 81 Lund Rd build three storeys where a 2013 zoning amendment (By-law 2015) had limited the land to two. About 240 units were envisioned. Two Westview Dr households asked about height, traffic through their neighbourhood, children's safety, drainage, privacy and fencing; L.S. asked that residents see the plan before approval. Council approved, noting the density was already allowed.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R26-132) subject to a development agreement. No commitment to show neighbours the design was recorded.
figures: About 240 units conceptually (minutes 11); 45-ft existing buffer (minutes 11).
reasons: meets-the-plan: already zoned RMD 13 years ago; height doesn't change density (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: L.S. and J.W. (Westview Dr) raised questions and concerns (minutes).
notes: Whether the 2013 two-storey limit responded to objectors then was not checked (outside period).

title: Six-storey seniors' building at 290 Stone Bridge Crossing approved 6-1; parking raised to 1.25
summary: V-2026-14 asked for six storeys (RMD allows three) and one stall per unit (1.5 required) for about 81 seniors' suites. No letters were filed, but residents of seven households spoke for over an hour, mostly about repeated sewer backups and flooding, plus traffic at school times, privacy, trees and property values. M.R. asked for an independent third-party study of Lift Station 1 and whether the developer's engineers were independent; the City Manager said they work under contract with the developer. The mayor kept steering the hearing back to height and parking. Council approved six storeys but raised parking to 1.25 per unit.
status_detail: Approved 6-1 (R26-147) at 1.25 stalls per unit instead of the 1 requested; Siemens's motion to deny died for want of a seconder. No third-party sewer study was offered.
figures: About 81 suites (minutes 16.6); parking 1.25/unit vs 1 requested and 1.5 required (R26-147).
reasons: need-housing: seniors on a 220-person waitlist; drainage can be fixed at the same time (Susan Penner); objections-not-planning-grounds: hearing is about height and parking; sewer handled by engineers and the development agreement (Mayor Earl Funk); already-consulted: being listened to is not the same as getting your way (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: M.R., G.K., B.K., A.A., M.N., D.J., D.F., G.R. and E.K. (seven households) objected or raised concerns (minutes; transcript).

title: William's Creek: 153-lot subdivision and rezoning approved; neighbours' requests not adopted
summary: By-law 2283 and subdivision 4451-2025-9083 created 153 lots (single-unit, duplex and multifamily) next to Wyndham and Ash Grove. Three households asked about drainage (two already flooded), fencing, green space, playgrounds, sidewalks, bus stops and traffic, and asked that lots 16-41/42 stay single-family. The developer said drainage was engineered with the city and that green space would be set in the development agreement. Council approved unchanged.
status_detail: Second reading (R26-156) and subdivision (R26-157) unanimous; the single-family request and 'forever fence' were not adopted.
figures: 153 lots (minutes).
reasons: meets-the-plan: parking, fencing and green space follow the zoning by-law and development agreement (developer / staff (minutes))
public: S.B., A.P. and G.W. raised questions and requests (minutes).
notes: Council debate not read in the transcript; minutes only. Third reading not found by Oct 20, 2026.

title: 12 units at 58 Giesbrecht St approved despite four neighbouring households' concerns
summary: By-law 2285 rezoned a large lot to RMD for a two-storey, 12-unit building. One letter was filed; K.V. and R.V., G.W., T.N. and H.K. raised privacy, trees, drainage, traffic and whether the city plans infill rather than reacting to developers. The applicant promised a fence, shielded lights, a drainage plan and to keep trees where possible. Council approved.
status_detail: Second reading unanimous (R26-179); third reading carried Oct 20, 2026 (transcript; minutes not yet available).
figures: 12 units, 2 storeys; 1 item of correspondence (minutes 7.2).
reasons: meets-the-plan: adjacent land already RMD; meets the by-law (Michael Zwaagstra); traffic-manageable: collector street built to take the traffic (applicant / Mayor Earl Funk)
public: K.V., R.V., G.W., T.N. and H.K. raised concerns (minutes).

title: 100 Kootenay Way setback variance approved; neighbour's garbage-bin request not met
summary: V-2026-19 reduced side yards from 20 ft to 4 ft in an RHD zone. A neighbour, E.K., asked that garbage bins be moved away from his house; the builder said they could not be moved. Council approved, adding a three-storey height limit.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R26-202) subject to a maximum of three storeys; the bin location was not changed.
public: E.K. (90 Kootenay Way) raised concerns (minutes).

title: 12-plex at 288 Henry St approved 6-1 after a neighbour's concerns; building moved back
summary: By-law 2286 and V-2026-16 (65-ft site width) allowed a 12-unit building next to the applicant's sixplex at 286 Henry. No letters were filed. C.M. (287 Henry) raised privacy, sunsets, trees, a big parking lot, snowbanks and ambulances, preferring a sixplex. The applicant said the building had been moved further back in response to his earlier comments.
status_detail: Approved 6-1 (R26-200, R26-201; Jake Hiebert against); third reading carried Oct 20, 2026 (transcript). The design change came before the hearing, from the applicant.
figures: 12 units, 20 stalls (minutes 27).
reasons: meets-the-plan: parking meets the by-law; no extra rules beyond it (Michael Zwaagstra); precedent: area in transition with RMD next door (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: C.M. raised concerns (minutes).

title: 330 McKenzie Ave rezoning denied unanimously after 62 letters and a full gallery
summary: By-law 2281 would have rezoned a 100 x 300 ft lot with a sound house to RMD for a two-storey, 20-unit building with 40 stalls and no variances; staff recommended approval. 34 items of correspondence were in the package and 28 more arrived that evening. About 12 people objected in person (character, trees, green space, traffic, children walking to school, precedent, property values; one asked council to 'remove the word integrity' from election signs if it approved) and one supported. Council denied it unanimously as not a transitional location; the mayor called it 'probably one of our best' public hearings.
status_detail: Second reading denied unanimously (R26-199). The clearest case in the period of objections changing the outcome against a staff recommendation.
figures: 62 items of correspondence (34 in package + 28 later; transcript 0:06:00, minutes 6.2); 20 units, 40 stalls (minutes 7).
public: A.N. and T.N. (adjacent), K.B., A.D., D.W., M.B., B.F., B.G., J.J., D.S., V.I. and M.H. objected or questioned; K.U. supported (minutes).
notes: Two other councillors spoke for denial (labels V and W, no speaker map); not quoted because they were not named before speaking.
